A claim circulating on social media suggests that Brazilian states and municipalities receive federal funding for every death attributed to COVID-19. This assertion, allegedly made by a nurse, has fueled debate and concern about the motivations behind COVID-19 data reporting in Brazil. To evaluate the veracity of this claim, it is necessary to examine the structure of federal health funding in Brazil, the mechanisms for COVID-19 financial support, and whether any direct financial incentives exist for reporting COVID-19 deaths.

Brazil’s public health system, known as the Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS), is financed by federal, state, and municipal governments. Federal funding is distributed based on population, epidemiological data, and specific health needs, but allocations are generally not tied to individual case or death numbers for specific diseases. Instead, the Ministry of Health uses broader metrics and periodic assessments to decide on funding amounts, aiming to strengthen general health services and respond to public health emergencies.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, the Brazilian federal government did provide extraordinary funding to states and municipalities to help combat the crisis. These funds were intended to expand hospital capacity, purchase medical supplies, and support testing and vaccination efforts. The allocation of emergency resources was based on factors such as population size, COVID-19 case numbers, and the overall needs of health systems in different regions. However, there is no evidence that funding was directly linked to the number of COVID-19 deaths reported by a state or municipality.

The claim that local governments receive money for “every death recorded” implies a per-death payment or bonus, which would create a perverse incentive to overreport fatalities. Official documentation and government statements do not support the existence of such a policy. Instead, funding decisions during the pandemic were made in response to the overall impact of the virus in each locality, which included case counts, hospitalizations, and health system capacity, but not a simple tally of deaths.

Furthermore, Brazil’s COVID-19 death reporting system involves multiple layers of verification. Deaths are recorded by hospitals and health professionals, reviewed by municipal and state health secretariats, and ultimately compiled at the federal level. This chain of reporting is designed to ensure accuracy and consistency, reducing the possibility of intentional misreporting for financial gain.

While it is true that states and municipalities with higher COVID-19 impact received more federal support, this was not a straightforward transaction based on the number of deaths. The support aimed to address increased health needs and the strain on local health systems, not to reward higher death tolls.

In conclusion, the claim that Brazilian states and municipalities earn federal funding for every COVID-19 death recorded is unfounded. Federal funding during the pandemic was allocated according to a range of epidemiological and logistical criteria, with no evidence of direct financial compensation for reported deaths. The suggestion that health authorities would be incentivized to misreport fatalities for monetary gain does not align with established funding mechanisms or public health practices in Brazil.

ဘရောက်စ်နိုင်ငံ၏ ကျန်းမာရေးစနစ်သည် စီမံခန့်ခွဲရေး စနစ်ကို ပြည်ထောင်စု၊ ပြည်နယ်နှင့် မြို့နယ် အစိုးရများက ငွေကိုယူပေးသည်။ ပြည်ထောင်စု ငွေကိုယူခြင်းများသည် လူဦးရေ၊ ကူးစက်နေသော ရောဂါအချက်အလက်များနှင့် ထူးခြားသော ကျန်းမာရေး လိုအပ်ချက်များအပေါ် အခြေခံ၍ ပေးအပ်ပေးသည်။ သို့သော် အမှန်တကယ် တစ်ရက်လျှင် အရေးကြီးသည့် ရောဂါနှင့် သေဆုံးမှုများအတွက် ကျော်လွန်သော ငွေကိုယူခြင်းများ အတွက် သာ အခြေခံမည်မဟုတ်ပါ။ ကျန်းမာရေး ဝန်ကြီးဌာနသည် ကျန်းမာရေး ဝန်ဆောင်မှုများကို တိုးတက်စေရန်နှင့် ကူးစက်နေသော ကျန်းမာရေး အကြိမ်ကြိမ်များအတွက် တိုးတက်စေရန် ပိုမို ကျယ်ပြန့်သော စံချိန်စံနှုန်းများနှင့် ပုံမှန် အကြံပြုချက်များကို အသုံးပြု၍ ငွေကိုယူခြင်းအား ဆုံးဖြတ်သည်။

ကိုဗစ်-၁၉ ရောဂါ အကြောင်းပြောပြရန် အတွက် ဘရောက်စ်နိုင်ငံ၏ ပြည်ထောင်စုအစိုးရသည် မျှော်လင့်ချက် ငွေကိုယူခြင်းကို ပြုလုပ်ခဲ့သည်။ ငွေကိုယူခြင်းကို ဆေးရုံများကို တိုးချဲ့ရန်၊ ဆေးဝါးများကို ဝယ်ယူရန် နှင့် စစ်ဆေးခြင်း နှင့် ကျွမ်းကျင်မှု အပြင်းအထိ အကူအညီပေးရန် ရည်ရွယ်ခဲ့သည်။ အခြေအနေ ငွေကိုယူခြင်းသည် လူဦးရေ အရေအတွက်၊ ကူးစက်နေသော ရောဂါ အရေအတွက် နှင့် အများအားဖြင့် ကျန်းမာရေး အစိုးရများကို အထူးသဖြင့် နေရာအမျိုးအစားများအတွက် ရှိနေသော လိုအပ်ချက်များ အပေါ် အခြေခံ၍ ပြုလုပ်ခဲ့သည်။ သို့သော် တစ်နိုင်ငံသည် သေဆုံးမှုအရေအတွက်ကို တစ်စုံတစ်ယောက် အကြောင်းပြောပြရန်အတွက် ငွေကိုယူခြင်းသည် မည်သည့် အထောက်အထားများကို ရှိသည်မဟုတ်ပါ။

နိုင်ငံတော်ကိုယ်စားလှယ်များကို "တစ်ကြိမ်တွင် တစ်ဦးချင်း သေဆုံးမှုအတွက် ငွေကိုယူခြင်း" ဟူ၍ ပြောခဲ့သော အကြောင်းအရာသည် အချက်အလက် သေဆုံးမှုအတွက် ငွေပေးခြင်း သို့မဟုတ် ပြောင်းလဲခြင်း ဖြစ်သည်။ ဤအရာကို ရှိသော ပြည်ထောင်စု အစိုးရ အစီအစဉ်များ သို့မဟုတ် တိကျသော ငွေပေးခြင်း အစီအစဉ်များကို မတည်ဆောက်ပါ။ ကိုဗစ်-၁၉ ကူးစက်ရောဂါ သေဆုံးမှုများကို ငွေကိုယူခြင်း အတွက် ငွေပေးခြင်းကို အသုံးပြုရန် အကြံပြုချက်များ မရှိပါ။ တစ်နိုင်ငံတွင် ကူးစက်နေသော ရောဂါကို ဖြစ်ပေါ်စေသည့် အထူးအကြောင်းအရာများကို ဖြစ်ပေါ်စေရန် အတွက် အထူးသဖြင့် ရောဂါ အကြိမ်ကြိမ်များ၊ ဆေးရုံ ကျန်းမာရေး သုံးစွဲမှုများနှင့် ကျန်းမာရေး စနစ် ဆုံးရှုံးမှုများကို စိစစ်ပေးခြင်းဖြင့် အမှန်တကယ် သေဆုံးမှုများကို ပြောပြရန် အတွက် တစ်နိုင်ငံတွင် မည်သည့် ပြည်ထောင်စု ငွေကိုယူခြင်းများကို အသုံးပြုခဲ့သည်မဟုတ်ပါ။

ပို၍ အထူးသဖြင့် ဘရောက်စ်နိုင်ငံတွင် ကိုဗစ်-၁၉ သေဆုံးမှုများကို အမှန်တကယ် မှန်ကန်စွာ အထူးသဖြင့် ရှိနေသည့် အခြေအနေများကို စစ်ဆေးရန် အထူးသဖြင့် အကြောင်းပြောပြရန် အတွက် မျှော်လင့်ချက် အစီအစဉ်များ ရှိသည်။ ဆေးရုံများနှင့် ကျန်းမာရေး ပညာရှင်များက သေဆုံးမှုများကို မှတ်တမ်းတင်ပြီး မြို့နယ်နှင့် ပြည်နယ် ကျန်းမာရေး အဖွဲ့အစည်းများက အထူးသဖြင့် မှန်ကန်စွာ စစ်ဆေးပြီး နောက်ဆုံးတွင် ပြည်ထောင်စု အဆင့်တွင် စုစည်းပေးသည်။ အခြေအနေများကို မှန်ကန်စွာ အထူးသဖြင့် တိကျစွာ အထူးသဖြင့် စိစစ်ရန် အတွက် အထူးသဖြင့် အမှန်တကယ် အခြေအနေများကို တိုးတက်စေရန် အတွက် အထူးသဖြင့် အမှားအယွင်းများကို အထူးသဖြင့် အမှီအခိုင်အမှုံးဖြင့် ပြုလုပ်နိုင်ခြင်းကို ပိုမို လျော့နည်းစေရန် ရည်ရွယ်ပါသည်။

အဆိုပါ အကြောင်းအရာမှာ ဘရောက်စ်နိုင်ငံ၏ ပြည်နယ်များနှင့် မြို့နယ်များကို ကိုဗစ်-၁၉ သေဆုံးမှုတစ်ခုချင်းစီအတွက် ပြည်ထောင်စုမှ ငွေကိုယူရန် မှန်ကန်စွာ မဟုတ်ပါ။ သို့သော် အခြေအနေများကို ပိုမို မှန်ကန်စွာ အထူးသဖြင့် တိကျစွာ စိစစ်ရန်အတွက် ပြည်ထောင်စုမှ ငွေကိုယူခြင်းအား ဖြစ်ပေါ်စေခဲ့သည်။ ကိုဗစ်-၁၉ ရောဂါ အကြောင်းပြောပြရန် အတွက် ပြည်ထောင်စုမှ ငွေကိုယူခြင်းအား ပိုမို အထူးသဖြင့် သေဆုံးမှုအရေအတွက်များကို အထူးသဖြင့် စိစစ်ရန် အတွက် ငွေပေးခြင်းများ ရှိသည်မဟုတ်ပါ။ ကျန်းမာရေး အစိုးရများသည် ငွေပေးခြင်းကို ပိုမို အထူးသဖြင့် အကြောင်းပြောပြရန် အတွက် ငွေပေးခြင်းကို အကြံပြုခြင်း မရှိပါ။
article_summary: O clamor de que estados e municípios brasileiros recebem verba federal por cada morte por COVID-19 é infundado. O financiamento federal durante a pandemia foi baseado em critérios epidemiológicos e logísticos, como população, necessidades de saúde e capacidade hospitalar, não em um sistema de pagamento por óbitos. Não há evidências de que a quantia recebida dependesse diretamente do número de mortes reportadas.
post_content: Nurse says Brazilian states and municipalities earn federal funding for every death recorded for COVID-19.

article_content:
A recent social media post has been circulating suggesting that individuals who begin to experience symptoms of COVID-19 should take azithromycin, ivermectin, and "Anitta" as part of their treatment. This claim has garnered attention and sparked debate, especially as misinformation regarding COVID-19 treatments remains a significant challenge worldwide. This article examines the validity of this claim by analyzing each component mentioned and providing context on current COVID-19 treatment recommendations.

The post references three substances: azithromycin, ivermectin, and Anitta. Azithromycin is an antibiotic commonly used to treat bacterial infections. Ivermectin is an anti-parasitic medication used to treat certain worm infestations and, in some cases, topical skin conditions. "Anitta" is ambiguous in this context; it could refer to a misspelling of "Anitta," a Brazilian pop star, or possibly a confusion with a medicine such as "Anitta" (a brand name for nitazoxanide, another anti-parasitic drug). However, there is no widely recognized COVID-19 treatment by the name "Anitta."

First, azithromycin has been studied for its potential use in treating COVID-19, primarily due to its anti-inflammatory properties and its ability to treat secondary bacterial infections that can occur along with viral illnesses. However, multiple large-scale clinical trials and expert health agencies have determined that azithromycin does not reduce the severity or duration of COVID-19 in patients who do not have a bacterial infection. The World Health Organization and most national health authorities do not recommend the routine use of azithromycin for COVID-19 unless there is a clear secondary bacterial infection.

Second, ivermectin gained popularity in some circles as a potential COVID-19 treatment early in the pandemic. However, rigorous scientific studies have not demonstrated a clear benefit of ivermectin in preventing or treating COVID-19. Health authorities, including the World Health Organization and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, do not recommend ivermectin for COVID-19 treatment outside of clinical trials. Inappropriate use of ivermectin, especially formulations intended for animals, has led to cases of toxicity and adverse health outcomes.

Third, "Anitta" as a treatment for COVID-19 does not appear in any recognized medical guidelines or scientific literature. If the post refers to "nitazoxanide," it is true that the drug has been studied for antiviral activity, but there is currently no robust evidence supporting its routine use for COVID-19.

Current best practice for treating COVID-19 involves supportive care, such as rest, hydration, and fever management. For individuals at higher risk of severe disease, such as older adults and those with certain underlying health conditions, medical professionals may prescribe antiviral medications authorized for COVID-19, such as nirmatrelvir/ritonavir or remdesivir, depending on the case and local guidelines. Importantly, early consultation with a healthcare professional is crucial, rather than self-medicating with unproven therapies.

In summary, the claim that people should take azithromycin, ivermectin, and "Anitta" at the onset of COVID-19 symptoms is not supported by current scientific evidence or official health guidelines. Individuals experiencing symptoms suggestive of COVID-19 should seek guidance from qualified healthcare providers rather than relying on unproven and potentially harmful treatments promoted on social media.

Nedavno je pojavila se društvena mreža koja preporučuje da ljudi koji počinju da iskazuju simptome kovida-19 uzmu azitromicin, ivermektin i "Anittu" kao dio liječenja. Ova tvrdnja je privukla pažnju i izazvala raspravu, posebno jer laži o liječenju kovida-19 ostaju značajna prepreka širom svijeta. Ovaj članak analizira važećnost ove tvrdnje, analizirajući svaku navedenu komponentu i pružajući kontekst trenutnih preporuka o liječenju kovida-19.

Post referira tri sastojka: azitromicin, ivermektin i Anitta. Azitromicin je antibiotik koji se često koristi za liječenje bakterijskih infekcija. Ivermektin je protivparazitarni lijek koji se koristi za liječenje određenih parazitskih infekcija i, u nekim slučajevima, za lokalne kožne stanje. "Anitta" je u ovom kontekstu ambijantan; može se odnositi na pogrešno napisano ime "Anitta", brazilske pop zvezde, ili možda pogrešnu asocijaciju s lijekom kao što je "Anitta" (brand name za nitazoksanid, drugi protivparazitarni lijek). Međutim, nema široko prepoznatog liječenja kovida-19 pod imenom "Anitta".

Prvo, azitromicin je istraživao se zbog mogućeg korištenja za liječenje kovida-19, pretežno zbog svojih protuupalnih svojstava i sposobnosti liječenja sekundarnih bakterijskih infekcija koje mogu nastati uz virusne bolesti. Međutim, više velikih kliničkih ispitivanja i stručni zdravstveni agencije su zaključili da azitromicin ne smanjuje težinu ili trajanje kovida-19 kod pacijenata koji nemaju bakterijsku infekciju. Svjetska zdravstvena organizacija (WHO) i većina državnih zdravstvenih službi ne preporučuje redovito korištenje azitromicina za kovida-19 osim ako postoji jasna sekundarna bakterijska infekcija.

Drugi, ivermektin je postao popularan u nekim krugovima kao potencijalno liječenje kovida-19 na početku pandemije. Međutim, stroga znanstvena istraživanja nisu pokazala jasnu prednost ivermektina u sprečavanju ili liječenju kovida-19. Zdravstvene službe, uključujući WHO i SAD i Food and Drug Administration (FDA), ne preporučuju korištenje ivermektina za liječenje kovida-19 osim u kliničkim ispitivanjima. Neprikladno korištenje ivermektina, posebno formulacija namijenjenih za životinje, dovelo je do slučajeva toksičnosti i štetnih zdravstvenih posljedica.

Treći, "Anitta" kao liječenje kovida-19 ne pojavljuje se u nijednom prepoznatljivom znanstvenom vodiču ili literaturi. Ako post referira na "nitazoksanid", istina je da je taj lijek istraživao za protivvirusnu aktivnost, ali trenutno nema dovoljno pouzdanih dokaza za njegovo redovno korištenje za kovida-19.

Trenutne najbolje prakse za liječenje kovida-19 uključuju podršku, poput odmora, hidratacije i upravljanja zatvorenim temperaturom. Za osobe s većim rizikom za ozbiljnu bolest, poput starijih osoba i onih s određenim osnovnim zdravstvenim stanjima, stručnjaci za zdravstvo mogu preporučiti antivirusne lijekove autorizirane za kovida-19, poput nirmatrelvira/ritonavira ili remdesivira, ovisno o slučaju i lokalnim vodičima. Važno je da je ranje konsultiranje s liječnikom ključno, umjesto da se liječi samostalno s neprovjerenim terapijama.

U zaključku, tvrdnja da ljudi treba uzeti azitromicin, ivermektin i "Anittu" na početku simptoma kovida-19 nije podržana trenutnim znanstvenim dokazima ili službenim zdravstvenim vodičima. Osobe koje iskazuju simptome koji ukazuju na kovida-19 treba da traže savjet od kvalificiranih zdravstvenih stručnjaka umjesto da se oslanjaju na neprovjerene i potencijalno štetne terapije promovirane na društvenim mrežama.

article_content:
A widely shared social media post claims that boldo tea and quina quina tea can prevent and even cure COVID-19. As misinformation continues to circulate during the pandemic, it is important to examine these claims critically and assess what is currently known about these herbal remedies and their effects on the coronavirus.

Boldo (Peumus boldus) is a plant native to South America, primarily Chile, whose leaves have long been used in traditional medicine for digestive disorders and liver ailments. Quina quina, commonly known as Cinchona, is a genus of plants famous for its bark, which contains quinine, a compound historically used to treat malaria. Both botanicals have storied histories in herbal medicine, but their purported benefits in relation to COVID-19 require close scrutiny.

The core claim in the social media post is twofold: that consuming teas made from boldo and quina quina can prevent infection with SARS-CoV-2, the virus responsible for COVID-19, and that these teas can cure those already infected. To evaluate this, it is essential to understand how COVID-19 is managed and what scientific evidence supports various treatments.

Currently, the World Health Organization and national health authorities emphasize that the best methods to prevent COVID-19 include vaccination, mask-wearing, hand hygiene, and physical distancing. Treatments for COVID-19 in clinical settings are based on robust research, including the use of antivirals, steroids, and supportive care. No herbal teas, including boldo or quina quina, are recognized as either preventive or curative treatments for COVID-19 by any major health authority.

Boldo tea contains compounds such as boldine and essential oils, which have demonstrated mild antimicrobial and antioxidant effects in laboratory studies. However, there is no evidence from clinical trials that boldo tea can prevent viral infections, including COVID-19. In fact, excessive consumption of boldo tea may lead to liver toxicity and other adverse effects, especially if used over extended periods or in large quantities.

Quina quina, or Cinchona bark, is the source of quinine, which was once a frontline treatment for malaria. Early in the pandemic, the related compound hydroxychloroquine was investigated for potential use against COVID-19, but multiple clinical trials eventually showed that it was not effective and could cause harmful side effects. The consumption of quina quina tea does not deliver a standardized or therapeutic dose of quinine, and there is no evidence that such teas can prevent or cure COVID-19.

In summary, while boldo and quina quina teas are traditional herbal remedies with certain uses in folk medicine, there is no scientific evidence to support the claim that they can prevent or cure COVID-19. Reliance on these teas instead of following evidence-based prevention and treatment guidelines could endanger health. As with all health information, it is critical to consult qualified healthcare professionals and rely on scientifically validated guidance during the pandemic.

A recent social media post claims that the World Health Organization (WHO) stated Coronavac, the COVID-19 vaccine developed by Sinovac Biotech, had not been tested anywhere in the world before its use in Brazil. This assertion has circulated widely on online platforms, leading to questions about Coronavac's development process and the global coordination of vaccine trials. A closer examination reveals that this claim is misleading and does not accurately reflect the facts about Coronavac’s testing history.

Coronavac is an inactivated virus vaccine developed by the Chinese pharmaceutical company Sinovac Biotech. It emerged as one of the leading COVID-19 vaccine candidates in 2020, alongside vaccines from other major global manufacturers. As with all vaccines, Coronavac underwent a series of clinical trials designed to assess its safety and efficacy before it could be widely distributed or administered to the public.

According to available information, Coronavac’s clinical development followed the standard three-phase process mandated for vaccine approval worldwide. Early-phase trials, including Phase 1 and Phase 2, were conducted in China beginning in April and May 2020. These initial studies focused on evaluating the vaccine’s safety profile and its ability to elicit an immune response in a controlled group of adult volunteers. The results from these early trials showed promising safety and immunogenicity data, paving the way for larger-scale studies.

Phase 3 clinical trials, which are crucial for assessing efficacy in preventing disease among diverse populations, were launched in several countries outside China. Notably, Brazil became a key site for Coronavac’s Phase 3 testing due to the high incidence of COVID-19 cases and the robust infrastructure for conducting large-scale clinical research. The Butantan Institute, a prominent biomedical research center in São Paulo, spearheaded the Brazilian trial beginning in July 2020, enrolling thousands of healthcare professionals.

However, Brazil was not the only country involved in Phase 3 testing. Indonesia and Turkey also hosted significant Coronavac trials involving thousands of participants. These parallel studies allowed Sinovac and regulatory bodies to gather a broad set of data on the vaccine’s effectiveness and safety across different populations and epidemiological contexts.

The World Health Organization, which is responsible for evaluating and prequalifying vaccines for global use, did not state that Coronavac had never been tested before its use in Brazil. Instead, the WHO monitored the progress of all vaccine candidates and reviewed data from trials in multiple countries before issuing any recommendations or approvals. In June 2021, Coronavac received emergency use listing from the WHO only after reviewing data from various international trials, including but not limited to those conducted in Brazil.

In conclusion, the claim that WHO said Coronavac had not been tested anywhere in the world before Brazil is inaccurate. Clinical trials for Coronavac began in China and were subsequently expanded to other countries, including Brazil. The WHO’s evaluation process relied on data from multiple studies, reflecting a coordinated international effort to test and validate the vaccine before its broader deployment.

उपलब्ध तपशीलानुसार, कोरोनावॅकची क्लिनिकल विकास प्रक्रिया वैक्सीन मंजूरीसाठी जगभरात अपेक्षित तीन टप्प्यांच्या प्रक्रियेनुसार घडली. प्रारंभिक टप्प्यांमध्ये, ज्यात टप्पा १ आणि टप्पा २ समाविष्ट होते, चीनमध्ये एप्रिल आणि मे २०२० मध्ये प्रारंभ केले गेले. या प्रारंभिक अभ्यासांचे ध्येय वैक्सीनच्या निरोगी वैशिष्ट्यांची आढळून आली आणि विशिष्ट संख्येतील वयस्क वॉलंटियर्समध्ये इम्यूनिटी उत्पन्न करण्याची क्षमता असल्याचे तपासणी करणे होते. या प्रारंभिक टप्प्यांचे निकाल उत्कृष्ट निरोगी आणि इम्यूनोजेनिसिटी डेटा दाखवत होते, ज्याने मोठ्या प्रमाणात अभ्यास चालू करण्याचा मार्ग दिला होता.

टप्पा ३ क्लिनिकल ट्रायल्स, जे विविध जनसंख्येत रोग रोध करण्याची प्रभावीता आढळून आली असल्याचे तपासणी करण्यासाठी आवश्यक आहेत, चीन बाहेरील काही देशांमध्ये सुरू झाले. खासकरून, ब्राझील जगभरातील कोविड-१९ मामल्यांची उच्च दर आणि मोठ्या प्रमाणात क्लिनिकल अभ्यास चालू करण्याची विशिष्ट आवश्यकता असल्याने कोरोनावॅकच्या टप्पा ३ टेस्टिंगचा मुख्य स्थळ बनला. सौ पाउलोमधील प्रमुख बायोमेडिकल अनुसंधान केंद्र बुटांटान इन्स्टिट्यूट जुलै २०२० मध्ये ब्राझीलच्या अभ्यासाचे नेतृत्व करत होते, ज्यामध्ये हजारों आरोग्य कर्मचारी भाग घेत होते.

हाय, ब्राझील एकमेव देश नव्हता ज्यामध्ये टप्पा ३ टेस्टिंग झाली. इंडोनेशिया आणि तुर्की देखील कोरोनावॅकच्या टेस्टिंगमध्ये विशिष्ट भूमिका बजावल्या गेल्या होत्या, ज्यामध्ये हजारों भागीदार आणि विविध जनसंख्येत एपिडेमियोलॉजिकल वातावरणात वैक्सीनची प्रभावीता आणि निरोगीता विश्लेषण करण्यासाठी तपासणी चालू झाली होती.

विश्व आरोग्य संगठन, जो वैक्सीनच्या वैश्विक वापरासाठी विश्लेषण आणि प्राथमिक अनुमती देण्याचे जबाबदार आहे, कोरोनावॅक ब्राझीलमध्ये वापरापूर्वी जगभरात कोणताही टेस्ट केलेला नसल्याचे नाही म्हटले आहे. त्याच वेळी, WHO ने सर्व वैक्सीन उमेदवारांच्या प्रगतीची निरीक्षण केली आणि विविध देशांमधील ट्रायल्सचे डेटा विश्लेषण केले आहे, त्यानंतरच त्यांनी कोणत्याही निर्माण किंवा मंजूरी दिली आहे. जून २०२१ मध्ये, कोरोनावॅक ला वैक्सीनच्या वैश्विक वापरासाठी आपत्कालीन वापर याची मंजूरी देण्यासाठी, विविध आंतरराष्ट्रीय ट्रायल्सचे डेटा विश्लेषण केले गेले, ज्यात ब्राझीलमधील ट्रायल्स असलेले असतील तर नाही.

खासगी निष्कर्ष म्हणजे, WHO ने कोरोनावॅकच्या ब्राझीलमध्ये वापरापूर्वी जगभरात कोणताही टेस्ट केलेला नसल्याचे म्हटले आहे असे दावा असतील तर ते असतील नाही. कोरोनावॅकच्या क्लिनिकल टेस्टिंग चीनमध्ये सुरू झाली आणि नंतर ब्राझील आणि इतर देशांमध्ये विस्तारित केली गेली. WHO चे विश्लेषण प्रक्रिया विविध अभ्यासांच्या डेटा आधारे आहे, जे वैक्सीनच्या व्यापक वितरणापूर्वी आंतरराष्ट्रीय प्रयत्नांचा परिणाम दर्शविते.

A claim circulating on social media suggests that prolonged use of masks can "acidify the blood," with a video of a doctor reportedly making this assertion. As mask-wearing remains a common public health measure, especially in healthcare settings and during respiratory illness outbreaks, it is important to examine the scientific validity of this claim.

Masks, including surgical masks and N95 respirators, are designed to block the spread of respiratory droplets, thereby reducing transmission of infectious diseases like COVID-19 and influenza. Since the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic, misinformation regarding mask safety has been widespread. One recurring theme is the suggestion that wearing a mask for extended periods can lead to harmful physiological effects, such as decreased oxygen levels or increased carbon dioxide retention.

The specific claim in question—mask use leading to "acidified blood"—implies a medical condition known as acidosis. Acidosis occurs when there is too much acid in the body fluids, which can result from respiratory or metabolic causes and may have serious health consequences if left untreated. Respiratory acidosis is typically caused by impaired lung function, leading to carbon dioxide buildup.

To evaluate the claim, it is necessary to understand how masks affect breathing. Scientific studies have investigated whether masks impede the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide. For healthy adults, wearing a mask does not significantly affect oxygen or carbon dioxide levels in the blood. Medical masks, including N95 respirators, are engineered to allow airflow while filtering particles. While minor discomfort or sensation of breathing resistance can occur, this does not translate into measurable changes in blood acidity for most people.

Healthcare workers routinely wear masks for hours at a time without evidence of blood acidification or related health problems. Even individuals with mild respiratory conditions generally tolerate mask use safely. In rare cases, those with severe pulmonary diseases may experience discomfort, and mask-wearing may need to be modified based on medical advice, but this is not due to blood acidification from mask use itself.

The assertion that "prolonged use of masks acidifies the blood" lacks scientific foundation. Current medical consensus and research do not support the idea that mask-wearing can induce acidosis or otherwise alter blood chemistry in healthy individuals. If a person experiences dizziness, shortness of breath, or other symptoms while wearing a mask, it is usually due to anxiety, improper mask fit, or unrelated health issues, not a dangerous change in blood acidity.

In summary, while online posts and videos may claim that extended mask use can acidify the blood, this assertion is not supported by credible medical evidence. Masks remain a safe and effective tool in infection prevention, and concerns about systemic blood chemistry changes from mask-wearing are unfounded for the vast majority of people. It is important to rely on evidence-based guidance from reputable health organizations when considering the risks and benefits of mask use.

article_content:
A recent social media post claims that a lottery employee in Brazil was recorded stealing COVID-19 emergency federal aid from a client. This allegation has generated significant attention online, prompting many to question the integrity of public service workers involved in the distribution of emergency funds during the pandemic.

To understand the context of this claim, it is important to recall that, during the COVID-19 pandemic, the Brazilian government implemented an emergency aid program known as Auxílio Emergencial. This program provided monthly payments to millions of low-income citizens who were economically affected by the crisis. Many Brazilians who did not have access to digital banking relied on state-sanctioned lottery agencies, known as “casas lotéricas,” to receive and withdraw these funds.

Lottery agencies, while privately operated, act as authorized agents of Caixa Econômica Federal, the government bank responsible for distributing the aid. These agencies have played a crucial role in ensuring that the emergency relief reached vulnerable populations, especially those without bank accounts or internet access. However, their frontline position has also raised concerns about potential irregularities and fraud.

The social media post alleges that a lottery employee was caught on camera stealing a client’s emergency aid. In fact, during the height of the Auxílio Emergencial disbursement, there were several reports across Brazil of clients claiming to have received less cash than they were entitled to, or of being misled during the withdrawal process. In some high-profile incidents, security camera footage did emerge showing employees pocketing portions of the cash meant for beneficiaries, usually by exploiting clients who were elderly, illiterate, or otherwise vulnerable.

Official investigations confirmed a handful of such cases, leading to the suspension or arrest of some lottery employees. These cases were treated seriously by both Caixa Econômica Federal and law enforcement, who urged beneficiaries to count their money before leaving the premises and to immediately report any discrepancies. Authorities also conducted audits and increased oversight at lottery outlets to curb such abuses.

However, it is important to note that the vast majority of lottery employees processed emergency aid payments without incident, and the documented theft cases represented a small fraction of the transactions. Nevertheless, the viral nature of the video evidence and the high public sensitivity surrounding emergency aid distribution amplified public concern.

In summary, the core claim that a lottery employee in Brazil was recorded stealing COVID-19 emergency federal aid from a client is accurate. While not widespread, such incidents did occur and were substantiated by video evidence and official investigations. The Brazilian government and Caixa Econômica Federal responded with increased oversight and public awareness campaigns to protect beneficiaries and maintain trust in the emergency aid system.

એક નવો સામાજિક મીડિયા પોસ્ટ માટે પ્રસ્તુત કરેલ દાવો છે કે બ્રાઝિલમાં લોટરી કર્મચારીએ કોવિડ-19 મહામારીના આંતરિક સરકારી સહાય માટે એક કસ્ટમરની મદદ કરી હતી. આ દાવાને ઑનલાઇન પર મોટી ધ્યાન આકર્ષિત કર્યું છે, જેથી ઘણા લોકોએ મહામારી દરમિયાન આંતરિક સહાય માટે સેવા આપતા સરકારી કર્મચારીઓની સમર્થતાની સંદેહ ઉભો કર્યો છે.

આ દાવાનો સાચો સંદર્ભ સમજવા માટે મહત્વપૂર્ણ છે કે કોવિડ-19 મહામારી દરમિયાન બ્રાઝિલ સરકારે એક આંતરિક સહાય યોજના તરીકે ઓળખાતી "એક્સ્યુલી એમરેજન્સિયલ" નામની યોજના લાગુ કરી હતી. આ યોજનાએ મહત્વપૂર્વક આર્થિક રૂપથી પ્રભાવિત માણસોને માસિક ભંડોળ આપ્યું હતું. ઘણા બ્રાઝિલિયનો ડિજિટલ બેંકિંગની પ્રવૃત્તિની ના ધરાવતા લોકોએ સ્થાનિય કેસા લોટરી એજન્સીઓ તરીકે ઓળખાતી સરકારના પ્રમાણિત લોટરી એજન્સીઓમાંથી આંતરિક સહાય મેળવી અને તેની વિસ્તાર કરી હતી.

લોટરી એજન્સીઓ, છતાં ખાસ કરીને સ્થાનિય કેસા લોટરી એજન્સીઓ તરીકે ઓળખાતી એટલે કે કેસા એકોનોમિક ફેડરલ સરકારના બેંકની અધિકૃત એજન્સીઓ તરીકે કામ કરે છે, જે આંતરિક સહાયનું વિતરણ કરે છે. આ એજન્સીઓએ આંતરિક સહાયની વિતરણ કરવામાં મુખ્ય ભૂમિકા ભજવી છે, ખાસ કરીને બેંકિંગ ખાતા અથવા ઇન્ટરનેટ પ્રવૃત્તિ ધરાવતા વ્યક્તિઓની મદદ કરવા માટે. તેમની મુખ્ય ભૂમિકા છતાં એ સંદેહનો વિષય પણ બની ગયો છે કે આ સંદર્ભમાં અસામાન્યતાઓ અથવા ધોંધાંધ સંભવિત છે.

સામાજિક મીડિયા પોસ્ટ માટે દાવો છે કે એક લોટરી કર્મચારીએ કેમેરામાં કેટલાક કસ્ટમરની આંતરિક સહાયની મદદ કરી હતી. વાસ્તવમાં, એક્સ્યુલી એમરેજન્સિયલ સહાયની વિતરણ સમયે, બ્રાઝિલમાં કેટલાક રિપોર્ટ્સ હતા જેમાં કેટલાક કસ્ટમરોએ તેમને જે માત્રાની સહાય આપવામાં આવી હતી તેની કરતાં ઓછી રકમ મળી હતી અથવા તેમની પ્રાપ્તિ પ્રક્રિયા દરમિયાન મોટા પ્રમાણમાં મોટા પ્રમાણમાં મોટા પ્રમાણમાં ભ્રમિત કરવામાં આવી હતી. કેટલાક મોટા મામલામાં, સુરક્ષા કેમેરાની ફોટોગ્રાફી પ્રકાશિત થઈ હતી જેમાં કર્મચારીઓએ કેટલાક પૈસાની મદદ કરી હતી જે લાભાર્થીઓની માટે માત્રા હતી, આમાંથી મોટા પ્રમાણમાં વૃદ્ધ, અક્ષમ અથવા અન્ય સંવેદનશીલ વ્યક્તિઓને ઉપયોગ કરી હતી.

અધિકૃત તપાસોએ અમુક મામલાની સાબિતી કરી હતી, જેથી કેટલાક લોટરી કર્મચારીઓની સ્થિતિ બંધ કરવામાં અથવા અટકાવવામાં આવી હતી. આ મામલાઓને કેસા એકોનોમિક ફેડરલ અને કાયદેસર અધિકારીઓએ ગંભીરતાથી લીધા હતા, જેઓ લાભાર્થીઓને તેમની રકમની જાંચ કરી અને પ્રાપ્તિ પછી કોઈપણ અસમાનતાની તપાસ કરવાની પ્રાર્થના કરી હતી. અધિકારીઓએ લોટરી સ્થાનોના પરીક્ષણ અને ઓવરસીટ વધારી દીધી હતી તાકી આવા અસામાન્યતાઓને રોકવા માટે.

તેમ છતાં, તે મહત્વપૂર્ણ છે કે લોટરી કર્મચારીઓએ મોટા ભાગની આંતરિક સહાય ભંડોળની કાર્યવાહીને સુધારી નથી અને સાક્ષ્ય દ્વારા નોંધાયેલ ચોરીના મામલાઓ કાર્યવાહીના માત્ર એક નાનો ભાગ હતા. તેમ છતાં, વિડિઓ પુરાવાનું વિરાલ સ્વરૂપ અને આંતરિક સહાયના વિતરણ પર મોટો સામાજિક સંવેદના આ �જાહેર ચિંતાને વધારી આપ્યું હતું.

સારાંશમાં, બ્રાઝિલમાં એક લોટરી કર્મચારીએ કોવિડ-19 મહામારીના આંતરિક સરકારી સહાયની મદદ કરી હતી તે દાવો સાચો છે. છતાં તે વિસ્તરીત નથી, અને આ ઘટનાઓ ઘટી હતી અને વિડિઓ પુરાવા અને અધિકૃત તપાસ દ્વારા સાબિત થઈ હતી. બ્રાઝિલની સરકાર અને કેસા એકોનોમિક ફેડરલે સામાજિક જાગૃતિ અભિયાનો અને આંતરિક સહાય સંસ્થાના સંભાવિત વિશ્વાસ રાખવા માટે ઓવરસીટ વધારી દીધી હતી.

Embora os casos confirmados sejam raros, a divulgação de evidências visuais ampliou o debate sobre a transparência no repasse de recursos públicos.

article_content:
In recent days, a social media post has circulated claiming that a hospital in the Brazilian city of Fortaleza has closed its Covid-19 ward due to a lack of patients. This statement has sparked discussion about the current state of the pandemic in Brazil and whether it reflects broader trends in Covid-19 case numbers and hospitalizations. This article examines the veracity of this claim and provides context regarding the pandemic's status in Fortaleza and Brazil as a whole.

Fortaleza, the capital of the northeastern state of Ceará, was one of the Brazilian cities hit hard by the Covid-19 pandemic in its early phases. Hospitals and emergency wards frequently operated at or beyond capacity, with patients experiencing long waits for beds and medical attention. As the pandemic evolved, the city implemented various public health measures, including vaccination campaigns, mask mandates, and restrictions on public gatherings. These efforts, combined with the national rollout of Covid-19 vaccines, contributed to a gradual decline in cases and hospitalizations over the past year.

The claim that a hospital in Fortaleza has closed its Covid-19 ward due to a lack of patients aligns with recent developments reported by local health authorities. With a significant portion of the population vaccinated and subsequent booster campaigns underway, the rate of severe Covid-19 cases requiring hospitalization has dropped substantially. In fact, several hospitals across Brazil, including those in Fortaleza, have begun to repurpose or close specialized Covid-19 units as patient numbers dwindle. This is seen as a positive milestone in the city’s public health response, reflecting the success of vaccination campaigns and other preventive measures.

However, it is important to note that the closure of a Covid-19 ward in one hospital does not mean the complete eradication of Covid-19 cases in Fortaleza or Brazil. Health officials remain vigilant, monitoring for potential surges or the emergence of new variants. Some hospitals maintain flexible protocols, allowing them to reopen specialized wards if necessary. Additionally, while the number of severe cases has decreased, mild and moderate cases may still occur, and outpatient services continue to provide care for those affected.

The closure of Covid-19 wards also highlights the transition of healthcare systems back to pre-pandemic service levels, reassigning resources to other critical areas such as elective surgeries, chronic disease management, and emergency care. It represents a significant shift in the pandemic’s trajectory, but does not signal a complete end to the need for Covid-19 precautions.

In conclusion, the central claim of the social media post—that a hospital in Fortaleza has closed its Covid-19 ward due to a lack of patients—is accurate according to current local health reports. The closure reflects a broader trend of declining Covid-19 hospitalizations, attributed to successful vaccination efforts and public health measures. Nevertheless, continued vigilance is advised, and health authorities remain prepared to respond to any future changes in the pandemic’s course.

અંગેના વાતાવરણમાં, એક સામાજિક મીડિયા પોસ્ટ ફરીથી પ્રસરણ કરી રહી છે કે બ્રાઝિલના ફોર્ટલેઝા શહેરમાં એક હોસ્પિટલે કોરોના વાયરસના બેડમાં પેશન્ટ્સની કમીને કારણે તેનું વિશેષ વિભાગ બંધ કરી દીધું છે. આ ઘોષણા બ્રાઝિલમાં કોરોના મહામારીની વર્તમાન સ્થિતિ અંગે ચર્ચા ઉત્પન્ન કરી છે અને તે કોરોના કેસની સંખ્યા અને હોસ્પિટલિઝેશનના વિસ્તૃત પ્રવાહ સાથે સંબંધિત છે. આ લેખ આ દાવાની સાચીતા પર વિચાર કરે છે અને ફોર્ટલેઝા અને બ્રાઝિલની મહામારીની સ્થિતિ અંગે સાંદ્રતા આપે છે.

ફોર્ટલેઝા, બ્રાઝિલમાં ઉત્તરપૂર્વ રાજ્ય સેરાના રાજધાની છે, જે મહામારીના પ્રારંભિક તબક્કામાં કોરોના વાયરસના ઘાતક પ્રભાવિત શહેરોમાંથી એક હતું. હોસ્પિટલો અને આંતરિક પ્રાથમિક સેવાઓ અને તેના ક્ષમતાની બહાર કામ કરતા રહેતા, જેથી પેશન્ટ્સ બેડ અને ચિકિત્સા માટે લાંબી રાહ જોવા પડતા. જ્યારે મહામારી વિકસે છે, ત્યારે શહેરે વિવિધ સામાજિક આરોગ્ય પ્રવૃત્તિઓને લાગુ કર્યું, જેમાં વેક્સીનેશન કેમ્પેઇન, માસ્ક કાયદાઓ અને જનસંખ્યાના સામૂહિક સંગ્રહની સીમાઓની નિયમનનો સમાવેશ થાય છે. આ પ્રયત્નો, સાથે રાષ્ટ્રીય સ્તરે કોરોના વાયરસ વેક્સીનેશન પ્રારંભિક પ્રવૃત્તિઓને સાથે લેવાથી, પ્રાથમિક વર્ષમાં કેસો અને હોસ્પિટલિઝેશન માટે સુધારો થયો હતો.

ફોર્ટલેઝામાં એક હોસ્પિટલનું કોરોના વાયરસના વિશેષ વિભાગ બંધ કરવાનો દાવો સ્થાનિક આરોગ્ય અધિકારીઓના પ્રાથમિક રિપોર્ટને અનુરૂપ છે. મોટા ભાગના લોકોને વેક્સીન આપવામાં આવ્યો છે અને તેના પછી વધારાના વેક્સીન કેમ્પેઇનો ચાલી રહી છે, જેથી હોસ્પિટલિઝેશન માટે ગંભીર કેસોની દર મોટા પ્રમાણમાં ઘટી ગઈ છે. વસ્તુતઃ, બ્રાઝિલમાં અનેક હોસ્પિટલો, ફોર્ટલેઝાના હોસ્પિટલો સહિત, કોરોના વાયરસના વિશેષ વિભાગોને પુનઃનિર્માણ કરી રહી છે અથવા બંધ કરી રહી છે કારણ કે રોગિયોની સંખ્યા ઘટી ગઈ છે. આ શહેરના આરોગ્ય પ્રતિક્રિયાનો એક સારો માર્કર માનવામાં આવે છે, જે વેક્સીન કેમ્પેઇન અને અન્ય પ્રતિરોધક પ્રવૃત્તિઓના સફળતાનો પ્રતિફળ છે.

તે છતાં, મહત્વપૂર્ણ છે કે એક હોસ્પિટલમાં કોરોના વાયરસના વિશેષ વિભાગનું બંધ થવું ફોર્ટલેઝા અથવા બ્રાઝિલમાં કોરોના કેસના પૂર્ણ નાશ નથી. આરોગ્ય અધિકારીઓ સતર્ક રહે છે, જે શક્ય ઉછાળની સંભાવના અથવા નવા વેરિયન્ટની ઉત્પત્તિને ધ્યાનમાં રાખે છે. કેટલાક હોસ્પિટલો સાથે નિર્ધારિત પ્રોટોકોલો સાથે કામ કરે છે, જે જરૂર પડે ત્યારે વિશેષ વિભાગોને પુનઃખોલવાની મંજૂરી આપે છે. વધુમાં, જો ગંભીર કેસોની સંખ્યા ઘટી ગઈ છે, તેમ છતાં, હળવા અને મધ્યમ કેસો હજુ પણ થઈ શકે છે, અને પ્રાથમિક રોગિયોની સેવાઓ પ્રભાવિત રોગિયો માટે સેવા આપે છે.

કોરોના વાયરસના વિશેષ વિભાગોના બંધ થવું પણ આરોગ્ય સિસ્ટમને મહામારી પહેલાના સેવા સ્તરો સુધી પાછો લેવા માટે પ્રસ્તુત કરે છે, અને સામાન્ય સર્જના, અસ્થમા સંબંધિત રોગોની પરિસ્થિતિ અને આંતરિક સેવાઓ જેવી અન્ય મહત્વપૂર્ણ ક્ષેત્રોમાં સંસાધનોનું પુનઃનિર્માણ કરે છે. તે મહામારીના પ્રવાહની એક મહત્વપૂર્ણ બદલાવનું પ્રતિફળ છે, પરંતુ કોરોના પ્રતિરોધક પગલાંની પૂર્ણ જરૂરિયાતનો અંત નથી જણાતો.

સંક્ષેપમાં, સામાજિક મીડિયા પોસ્ટનો મુખ્ય દાવો કે ફોર્ટલેઝામાં એક હોસ્પિટલે કોરોના વાયરસના વિશેષ વિભાગનું બંધ કરી દીધું છે કારણ કે રોગિયોની સંખ્યા ઓછી છે તે સ્થાનિક આરોગ્ય રિપોર્ટ્સ મુજબ સાચો છે. વિશેષ વિભાગનું બંધ થવું મહામારીના હોસ્પિટલિઝેશનની ઘટનાનો વિસ્તૃત પ્રવાહનો પ્રતિફળ છે, જે સફળ વેક્સીન પ્રયત્નો અને સામાજિક આરોગ્ય પ્રવૃત્તિઓને કારણે થયો છે. તેમ છતાં, આગળની મહામારીની પ્રવૃત્તિઓની બદલાવ સામે સતર્કતા જણાવવામાં આવે છે, અને આરોગ્ય અધિકારીઓ તેની સામે કોઈપણ વિસ્તારની પ્રવૃત્તિઓની તૈયારી રાખે છે.

In the midst of the COVID-19 pandemic, discussions about potential treatments and regulatory decisions have been the subject of much debate and misinformation. A recent social media post claims, “By revoking the permission to use chloroquine in hospitalized patients, the FDA expanded the use of the drug in the USA.” This statement raises questions about the actual actions taken by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regarding chloroquine, and whether revoking its use in certain contexts truly expanded its application elsewhere.

To evaluate this claim, it is important to understand the role of chloroquine and its related drug, hydroxychloroquine, during the COVID-19 crisis. Early in the pandemic, these drugs—originally developed to treat malaria and certain autoimmune conditions—were considered potential treatments for COVID-19. Based on preliminary laboratory studies and limited clinical data, the FDA issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) in March 2020, allowing hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine to be used in hospitalized COVID-19 patients when clinical trials were unavailable.

However, as more rigorous clinical studies emerged, evidence increasingly showed that these drugs were not effective in treating COVID-19 and could cause serious side effects, including heart rhythm problems. In June 2020, the FDA revoked the EUA for hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine for hospitalized patients, citing a lack of efficacy and potential risks.

The social media claim suggests that by revoking this authorization, the FDA somehow broadened the use of chloroquine in the U.S. This interpretation misrepresents the FDA’s actions and their consequences. The revocation of the EUA specifically limited the use of chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine for treating COVID-19 in hospitalized settings. It did not expand their use for COVID-19, nor did it authorize or encourage their broader application in outpatient or other populations.

Outside the context of COVID-19, chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine have long-standing approvals for other indications, such as malaria, lupus, and rheumatoid arthritis. These uses were unaffected by the FDA’s COVID-19-specific rulings. The revocation did not impact prescribing for those conditions, but it did restrict the drugs’ emergency access for COVID-19 patients.

It is also important to note that while physicians in the United States may prescribe approved drugs “off-label” for conditions not specifically listed in the approval, the FDA’s revocation sent a clear signal regarding the lack of evidence for use against COVID-19. Major health organizations and medical societies subsequently advised against using these drugs for COVID-19 outside of clinical trials.

In summary, the claim that revoking permission for chloroquine in hospitalized patients expanded its use in the USA is inaccurate. The FDA’s revocation of the EUA for chloroquine in COVID-19 patients represented a restriction, not an expansion, of its authorized use during the pandemic. The regulatory decision narrowed the scope for which the drug could be used in COVID-19, aligning with evolving scientific evidence and patient safety concerns.

U sredini pandemije kovida-19, rasprave o potencijalnim liječenjima i regulatornim odlukama bile su predmet mnogih rasprava i lažnih informacija. Nedavna objava na društvenim mrežama tvrdi: „Uklanjanjem dopuštenja za upotrebu klorokuina kod bolesnika u bolnicama, FDA je proširio upotrebu lijeka u SAD-u.“ Ova tvrdnja podiže pitanje o stvarnim akcijama U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) u vezi s klorokuinom, te je li uklanjanje njegove upotrebe u određenim kontekstima zaista proširilo njeno primjene u drugim područjima.

Da bi ocijenili ovu tvrdnju, važno je razumjeti ulogu klorokuina i povezanog lijeka, hidroksiklorokuina, tijekom pandemije kovida-19. Na početku pandemije, ovi lijekovi, koji su pored toga razvijeni za liječenje malarije i određenih autoimunih bolesti, bili su smatrani potencijalnim liječenjem za kovida-19. Na temelju primitivnih laboratorijskih studija i ograničenih kliničkih podataka, FDA je 2020. otkazao autorizaciju za neposrednu upotrebu (EUA), omogućujući upotrebu hidroksiklorokuina i klorokuina kod bolesnika s kovida-19 u bolnicama kada su klinički ispitivanja nedostupna.

Međutim, kako su se pojavile stroži klinički studiji, dokazi su sve više pokazivali da su ovi lijekovi neefikasni u liječenju kovida-19 i mogli su uzrokovati ozbiljne strane efekte, uključujući probleme s ritmom srca. U juni 2020., FDA je otkazao autorizaciju za neposrednu upotrebu hidroksiklorokuina i klorokuina za bolesnike u bolnicama, navodeći nedostatak efikasnosti i potencijalne rizike.

Tvrdnja na društvenim mrežama pretpostavlja da je otkazivanje ove autorizacije nešto što je proširilo upotrebu klorokuina u SAD-u. Ova interpretacija netočno predstavlja djelovanje FDA-a i njegove posljedice. Otkazivanje autorizacije za neposrednu upotrebu specifično je ograničilo upotrebu klorokuina i hidroksiklorokuina za liječenje kovida-19 kod bolesnika u bolnicama. Nije proširilo njihovu upotrebu za kovida-19, niti je autoriziralo ili potaknulo njihovu šire primjenu u ambulantnim ili drugim populacijama.

Van konteksta kovida-19, klorokuin i hidroksiklorokuin imaju dugotrajna odobrenja za druge indikacije, poput malarije, lupusa i reumatoidnog artritisa. Ove upotrebe nisu bile utjecajne na FDA-ove odluke specifične za kovida-19. Otkazivanje nije utjecalo na prepišivanje za te bolesti, ali je ograničilo hitnu dostupnost lijekova za bolesnike s kovida-19.

Također je važno napomenuti da je u SAD-u liječnici mogli prepišivati odobrene lijekove „neformalno“ za bolesti koje nisu specifično navedene u odobrenju. Otkazivanje FDA-a je poslalo jasno poruku o nedostatku dokaza za upotrebu protiv kovida-19. Veliki zdravstveni organizacije i medicinska udruženja nakon toga su preporučila izbjegavanje upotrebe ovih lijekova za kovida-19 izvan kliničkih ispitivanja.

U skladu s tim, tvrdnja da je otkazivanje dopuštenja za upotrebu klorokuina kod bolesnika u bolnicama proširilo njegovu upotrebu u SAD-u netočna. Otkazivanje autorizacije za neposrednu upotrebu klorokuina za bolesnike s kovida-19 predstavljalo je ograničenje, a ne proširenje, njegove odobrene upotrebe tijekom pandemije. Regulacijska odluka je smanjila opseg upotrebe lijeka za kovida-19, uskladila se s evolucijom znanstvenih dokaza i zdravstvenim brinom za pacijente.

A social media post circulating widely claims that Brazilian hospitals receive R$ 18,000 for each death registered as "suspected COVID-19." This assertion has generated significant public concern, raising questions about hospital funding, the accuracy of COVID-19 data, and the integrity of the healthcare system in Brazil. A thorough review of the facts and context behind this claim reveals a more nuanced reality.

The allegation suggests that hospitals have a financial incentive to attribute deaths to COVID-19, even when the diagnosis is only suspected and not confirmed. This type of claim has appeared in several countries since the start of the pandemic, often fueling conspiracy theories and distrust in public health statistics.

To understand the basis of the claim, it is essential to examine how hospital funding works in Brazil, particularly in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. Brazil's public healthcare system, known as the Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS), is responsible for providing medical care to the population, and it receives funding from both federal and state sources. During the pandemic, the government implemented various measures to support hospitals, including additional financial resources to manage the surge in cases and the increased burden on the healthcare system.

One significant measure was the provision of extra funding for hospitals treating COVID-19 patients, particularly for those requiring intensive care. The Brazilian Ministry of Health authorized payments to hospitals for each COVID-19 patient admitted to an Intensive Care Unit (ICU). The amount paid per ICU bed per day was increased to ensure hospitals could cover the costs associated with the specialized care required during the pandemic. In some instances, the daily payment for an ICU bed for COVID-19 patients reached approximately R$ 1,600. If a patient remained in the ICU for an extended period, the total cost per patient could reach or exceed R$ 18,000, but this amount was not paid per death or per suspected COVID-19 case.

Crucially, there is no official policy or mechanism by which hospitals receive a lump sum of R$ 18,000 simply for registering a death as "suspected COVID-19." Payments to hospitals are based on the care provided, particularly in the ICU, and are not directly tied to the cause of death. Moreover, the Brazilian Ministry of Health requires hospitals to report deaths according to strict criteria, and "suspected COVID-19" is only used when there is clinical or epidemiological evidence of the disease but laboratory confirmation is pending or unavailable.

Experts and health authorities have consistently denied that there is any systemic incentive for hospitals to falsely attribute deaths to COVID-19 in order to receive extra funding. While the government did provide increased resources to hospitals during the pandemic, these were intended to support the extraordinary costs of care, not to reward the reporting of COVID-19 deaths.

In conclusion, the claim that Brazilian hospitals receive R$ 18,000 for each death registered with "suspected COVID-19" is misleading. While hospitals did receive increased funding related to the care of COVID-19 patients, payment structures are based on services rendered, not on the registration of deaths. There is no evidence of a direct financial incentive tied specifically to deaths registered as suspected COVID-19.

ソーシャルメディアで広く拡散されている投稿によると、ブラジルの病院は「疑いのコロナウイルス（COVID-19）」として記録された死亡ごとに18万レアルを支払われているという。この主張は大規模な公の関心を引き、病院の資金調達、COVID-19データの正確性、およびブラジルの医療制度の信頼性に関する疑問を生じさせている。この主張の背景にある事実と文脈を慎重に検証すると、より複雑な現実が明らかになる。

この主張は、診断が疑いのみで確定されていないにもかかわらず、病院がコロナウイルスによる死亡を記録することで金銭的なインセンティブがあると主張している。この種の主張は、パンデミックが始まって以来、いくつかの国で登場しており、しばしば陰謀論や公衆衛生統計への不信感を煽っている。

この主張の根拠を理解するには、特にパンデミック下でのブラジルの病院資金調達の仕組みを検討することが重要である。ブラジルの公共医療制度である「統一保健システム（SUS）」は、住民に医療サービスを提供し、連邦政府および州政府から資金を提供を受けている。パンデミック期間中には、政府は病院への支援として、症例の増加や医療システムへの負担に対応するための追加的な財政的支援を実施した。これには、コロナウイルス患者を治療する病院に特別な資金を提供する措置も含まれていた。

重要な措置の一つは、コロナウイルス患者を治療する病院への追加資金の提供であり、特に重症患者を治療する病院に対して支払われた。ブラジル保健省は、コロナウイルス患者が集中治療室（ICU）に収容された場合、各ICUベッドごとに支払いを行うことを許可した。パンデミックの特需に対応するため、ICUベッドごとの日額支払い額を増加させた。一部のケースでは、コロナウイルス患者のICUベッドの日額支払いは約1万6千レアルに達した。患者がICUに長期間滞在した場合、1人の患者あたりの総額は18万レアルに達するかそれ以上になる可能性があるが、これは死亡ごとにではなく、疑いのコロナウイルス症例ごとに支払われるものではない。

重要な点として、病院が「疑いのコロナウイルス」として記録された死亡ごとに18万レアルを一括して受け取るという公式な政策や仕組みは存在しない。病院への支払いは、特にICUでの医療サービスに基づいて行われており、直接的に死因と関連付けられているわけではない。また、ブラジル保健省は病院に対し、厳格な基準に基づいて死亡を報告するよう求めている。そして、「疑いのコロナウイルス」は、検査結果が未確認または入手できない場合でも、臨床的または疫学的な証拠がある場合にのみ使用される。

専門家や医療当局は、病院が金銭的なインセンティブを受けてコロナウイルスによる死亡を虚偽で報告するというシステム的な動機があると否定している。政府はパンデミック期間中、病院に対して追加の資源を提供したが、これは医療の特需に伴う費用を補填するためのものであり、コロナウイルス死亡の報告を報酬としているものではない。

結論として、ブラジルの病院が「疑いのコロナウイルス」として記録された死亡ごとに18万レアルを支払われているという主張は誤解を招くものである。病院はコロナウイルス患者の治療にかかわる追加資金を受け取ったが、支払いは提供されたサービスに基づいており、死亡の記録とは直接関係ない。疑いのコロナウイルスとして記録された死亡に特化した直接的な金銭的インセンティブの証拠は存在しない。

The claim circulating on social media states that the Mayor of São Paulo, after being diagnosed with COVID-19, used chloroquine—a drug that, according to the post, was banned by the municipal government. This assertion has caused confusion and debate, especially considering the contentious role of chloroquine in COVID-19 treatment protocols and public health policies in Brazil.

Chloroquine and its derivative, hydroxychloroquine, gained international attention early in the COVID-19 pandemic as potential treatments for the virus. This interest was sparked by preliminary studies and amplified by political leaders, both in Brazil and globally. However, as more rigorous clinical trials were conducted, the scientific consensus shifted: major health authorities, including the World Health Organization, concluded that chloroquine did not provide benefits in treating COVID-19 and posed risks of serious side effects. Consequently, many governments and medical bodies updated their guidelines, advising against the use of chloroquine for COVID-19 patients outside of clinical trials.

In Brazil, the debate over chloroquine became highly politicized. Some federal authorities promoted its use, while many local governments and health professionals expressed concern over its safety and efficacy. In São Paulo, the municipal administration aligned with the broader scientific consensus. The city’s health department did not formally "ban" chloroquine, but it restricted its use to specific clinical circumstances and did not recommend it as part of the official COVID-19 treatment protocol in public hospitals. This distinction is crucial: restricting a drug’s use based on clinical guidelines is different from an outright ban.

Turning to the mayor himself, there have been reports regarding the health of São Paulo’s mayor during the pandemic. If the mayor did contract COVID-19 and was treated with chloroquine, this would raise questions about adherence to official health recommendations and transparency. However, public records and statements from the mayor’s office indicate that while the mayor did test positive for COVID-19, there is no verifiable evidence that he received chloroquine as a treatment. In interviews and press releases, the mayor stated that he followed medical advice and adhered to treatment protocols recommended by his healthcare team, which were in line with municipal and national guidelines at the time.

Moreover, even if an individual public official were to use a treatment not recommended in public health guidelines, this would not constitute a violation of a "ban," unless there was a legal or regulatory prohibition on prescribing or using the drug. In the case of São Paulo, no such absolute ban was in place; rather, there were strong recommendations based on current medical evidence.

In summary, the claim that the mayor of São Paulo used chloroquine after a COVID-19 diagnosis, despite a municipal ban, is misleading. While the city’s health authorities did not recommend chloroquine and restricted its use, there was no outright prohibition. Additionally, there is no confirmed evidence that the mayor himself used the drug. This post exemplifies how nuanced public health guidance can be distorted or oversimplified in social media discourse, underscoring the need for careful fact-checking and context.

Hierdie bewering het verwarring en debat veroorsaak, veral omdat chloroquine se kontroversiële rol in die behandelingsprotokolle en gesondheidsbeleid vir COVID-19 in Brasilië belangrik is.

Chloroquine en sy afgeleide, hydroxychloroquine, het vroeg in die COVID-19 pandemie internasionale aandag gekry as moontlike behandelings vir die virus. Hierdie belangstelling is geweek in deur voorlopige studies en versterk deur politieke leiers, sowel in Brasilië as mondryk. Echter, ná meer rigiede kliniese studies, het die wetenskaplike konsensus verander: groot gesondheidsinstansies, insluitend die Wêreldgesondheidsorganisasie, het geconkludeer dat chloroquine geen voordadele bied in die behandeling van COVID-19 nie en dat dit risiko's van ernstige neerslag het. Daarom het baie regeringe en mediese instansies hul riglyne aangepas, en het hulle aangewys dat chloroquine nie aanbevolen moet word vir pasiënte met COVID-19 nie, behalwe binne kliniese studies.

In Brasilië het die debat oor chloroquine baie politieke dimensies gekry. Sommige federale autoriteite het sy gebruik bevorder, terwyl baie lokale regeringe en gesondheidsprofessionals besorgd was oor sy veiligheid en doeltreffendheid. In São Paulo het die stadse beheer ondersteun die breër wetenskaplike konsensus. Die stad se gesondheidsdepartement het nie formel 'n verbod op chloroquine uitgeklaar nie, maar het sy gebruik beperk tot spesifieke kliniese omstandighede en het dit nie aanbevolen as deel van die offisiële COVID-19 behandelingsprotokol in openbare hospitale nie. Hierdie onderskeiding is belangrik: die beperking van 'n middel se gebruik op grond van kliniese riglyne is verskil van 'n volledige verbod.

Wat betreft die baas self, is daar verslaggewing oor sy gesondheid tydens die pandemie. Indien die baas inderdaad besmet was met COVID-19 en chloroquine gebruik het, sal dit vrae oor volgeling van offisiële gesondheidsraad en transparantie oproep. Echter, openbare dokumente en stellings van die baas se kantoor dui daarop dat die baas wel positief geteester het vir COVID-19, maar daar is geen bewyse wat bevestig dat hy chloroquine as behandeling ontvang het nie. In interviews en persverklarings het die baas verklaar dat hy mediese raad gevolg en aanbevolen protokolle gevolg het wat deur sy gesondheidskragte aangebied is, wat inlyn was met stadse en nasionale riglyne op daardie tydstip.

Besoekens, selfs as 'n openbare funksioneerder 'n behandeling gebruik wat nie aanbevolen word in gesondheidsriglyne nie, sal nie 'n oortreding van 'n "verbod" wees nie, tenzij daar 'n wettige of regulere verbod op die voorskrif of gebruik van die middel was. In die geval van São Paulo was daar geen absolute verbod nie; eerder was daar sterke aanbevelings gebaseer op huidige mediese bewyse.

In die samenvatting, die bewering dat die baas van São Paulo chloroquine gebruik het ná 'n diagnose van COVID-19, ondanks 'n stadse verbod, is misleidend. Terwyl die stad se gesondheidsautoriteite chloroquine nie aanbevolen het en sy gebruik beperk het nie, was daar geen volledige verbod nie. Daar is ook geen bevestigde bewyse dat die baas self die middel gebruik het nie. Hierdie stelling illustreer hoe nuanserde gesondheidsraad deur sosiale media geïnterpreteer of vereenvoudig kan word, wat die noodsaaklikheid benadruk van akkurate feitbeskakeling en konteks.

The claim that “prolonged use of masks causes lack of oxygenation” has circulated widely on social media, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic, as mask mandates became common in public spaces. This assertion has caused concern among some members of the public, leading to hesitancy or resistance to mask-wearing. To assess the validity of this claim, it is important to examine the context of mask usage, the science behind mask design, and the evidence from studies and medical institutions.

Masks, including surgical masks, cloth face coverings, and N95 respirators, have been recommended by health authorities to reduce the transmission of respiratory illnesses, notably COVID-19. Their primary function is to block respiratory droplets that may contain viruses, thereby protecting both the wearer and those nearby. The claim under scrutiny suggests that wearing masks for extended periods impairs oxygen intake, potentially leading to hypoxia (low blood oxygen levels).

Medical experts and organizations have consistently stated that masks made for public use are designed to be breathable and do not restrict oxygen flow. The materials used in surgical and cloth masks are permeable to air and allow for normal gas exchange. N95 respirators, while providing a higher level of filtration, are still intended to allow adequate airflow for healthy individuals during routine activities. The sensation of discomfort or warmth that some people report while wearing masks is generally attributed to trapped heat or moisture rather than a lack of oxygen.

Numerous studies have tested the effects of mask-wearing on oxygen and carbon dioxide levels. These studies have typically involved health care workers and members of the public wearing various types of masks in both clinical and real-world settings. The results consistently show that oxygen saturation in the blood remains within normal ranges, even during prolonged use of masks. Some studies have explored mask use during physical activity, and while masks may cause a slight perception of increased effort, they do not result in dangerous drops in oxygen levels for healthy individuals.

It is important to note that certain individuals with pre-existing respiratory conditions may experience discomfort while wearing masks. In these cases, medical guidance should be sought. However, for the vast majority of people, mask-wearing is safe and does not compromise oxygenation.

In conclusion, the claim that prolonged use of masks causes a lack of oxygenation is not supported by scientific evidence. Masks are designed to be breathable and safe for extended wear by healthy individuals. The discomfort some may feel is not indicative of insufficient oxygen intake. Public health guidance continues to support mask-wearing as an effective measure to prevent the spread of respiratory illnesses without posing a risk of hypoxia. As always, individuals with specific medical concerns should consult healthcare professionals for personalized advice.

Пријава да "дуготрајно коришћење маски изазива недостатак оксигенације" широм се распространила на социјалним мрежама, посебно током пандемије коронавируса, када су маске постале обавезне у јавним просторима. Ово изјава је изазвала тревогу код неких чланова јавности, што је довело до несигурности или отпора у коришћењу маски. Да бисмо проценили важност ове изјаве, важно је да проучимо контекст коришћења маски, научну основу дизајна маски и доказе из студија и медицинских институција.

Маске, укључујући хируршке маске, крпене заштитне маске и N95 дихателне маске, препоручиване су здравственим органима да се смањи пренос дихалних болести, према томе коронавируса. Основна функција маски је да спрече дихалне капљице које могу садржати вирусе, што заштити носиоца и онога ко је близу. Изјава која се прегледа сугерише да дуготрајно носење маски утиче на усисавање кисеоника, што би могло довести до хипоксије (ниских нивоа кисеоника у крви).

Медички експерти и организације су увек наводили да су маске које се користе у јавности дизајниране да буду дихајуће и да не ограничавају ток кисеоника. Материјали који се користе у хируршким и крпеним маскама су пропусни за ваздух и омогућавају нормалну гасну експрезију. N95 дихателне маске, наравно, пружају већу ниво филтрирања, али је увијек намењене да омогуће довољан ток ваздуха за здраве особе током обичних активности. Неудобност или топлота коју неки луѓе осете при носењу маски углавном је повезана са застајућом топлотом или влагом, а не са недостатком кисеоника.

Многе студије су испитивале ефект носења маски на ниво кисеоника и угљен диоксид. Ове студије су углавном укључивале здравствене раднике и чланове јавности који су носили различите врсте маски и у клиничким и стварним условима. Резултати се конзистентно поклопили са том да се ниво сатурације кисеоника у крви одржава у нормалним границама, чак и при дуготрајном коришћењу маски. Неке студије су истраживале коришћење маски током физичке активности, а макар маске могу изазвати леку осетљивост на повећану улогу, не доводе до опасних падова нивоа кисеоника за здраве особе.

Важно је напоменути да одређени луђе са претходним дихалним болнима могу извести неудобност при носењу маски. У овим случајевима треба потражити медицинску консултацију. Међутим, за већину људи, носење маски је безбедно и не умањује оксигенацију.

У закључку, изјава да дуготрајно коришћење маски изазива недостатак оксигенације није подржана научним доказима. Маске су дизајниране да буду дихајуће и безбедне за дуготрајно коришћење здравих особа. Неудобност коју неки осете није индикативна за недостатак усисавања кисеоника. Здравствена пракса наставља да подржава носење маски као ефективну меру за спречавање преноса дихалних болести без ризика од хипоксије. Како увек, особе са специфичним медицинским проблемима треба да консултују здравствене професионале за персонализовану консултацију.

In recent years, Brazil has faced significant challenges in managing the COVID-19 pandemic, with political tensions and legal battles shaping the country’s response. A social media post claims that the Brazilian Supreme Court ruled President Jair Bolsonaro could not determine actions to combat the pandemic. This article examines the accuracy of this statement, providing context and analysis of the Supreme Court’s role in Brazil’s pandemic response.

The core of the claim refers to a pivotal decision made by the Supreme Federal Court (Supremo Tribunal Federal, or STF) in April 2020, shortly after the COVID-19 outbreak began affecting Brazil. At that time, President Bolsonaro’s administration advocated for a centralized approach, seeking to limit restrictive measures such as lockdowns and quarantines, which Bolsonaro argued were damaging to the economy. Several governors and mayors, however, sought to implement stricter public health measures in their respective regions, citing rising infection rates and concerns over hospital capacity.

Tensions escalated as the federal government attempted to assert authority over local and state governments’ pandemic responses. In response to petitions from various states, the Supreme Court reviewed the constitutionality of actions taken by both state and federal authorities. The STF ruled that the federal government could not override the powers of states and municipalities to implement health-related measures, such as social distancing, lockdowns, and mask mandates. The Court clarified that the federal, state, and municipal governments all share responsibility for public health policy, but that local authorities retain autonomy to combat the pandemic as they see fit within their jurisdictions.

This ruling did not strip President Bolsonaro of all influence over pandemic policy. The federal government remained responsible for nationwide strategies, such as vaccine procurement, funding for health services, and guidance from the Ministry of Health. However, the decision blocked any attempts by the President to prevent governors and mayors from enacting stricter local measures, effectively limiting his unilateral control over pandemic combat actions.

The Supreme Court’s decision was rooted in Brazil’s constitutional framework, which establishes a decentralized approach to public health and emergency management. The ruling underscored the importance of regional authorities being able to react swiftly to local conditions, independent of federal directives that might not account for specific needs or circumstances.

In evaluating the claim from the social media post, it is accurate to state that the Brazilian Supreme Court ruled President Bolsonaro could not solely determine actions to combat the pandemic. The decision ensured local and state governments could act independently, even if those actions conflicted with the President’s preferences or official policy. While Bolsonaro maintained some authority over federal pandemic response, his ability to dictate nationwide measures was constitutionally constrained by the Supreme Court’s ruling.

In summary, the Supreme Court’s intervention was a significant moment in Brazil’s pandemic response, safeguarding the autonomy of regional governments and preventing President Bolsonaro from unilaterally controlling all actions to combat COVID-19. The social media claim reflects the reality of this legal and political development.

A recent social media post claims that individuals experiencing symptoms of COVID-19 should self-medicate with chloroquine and azithromycin, and also take zinc and vitamins C and D supplements. This claim encourages specific drug use and supplements as a self-management approach to COVID-19 symptoms. A careful examination of current medical guidance and scientific evidence is necessary to assess the accuracy and safety of this advice.

Chloroquine and azithromycin both attracted attention early in the COVID-19 pandemic. Chloroquine, traditionally used to treat malaria, and its related compound, hydroxychloroquine, were initially studied for their potential antiviral effects. Azithromycin, an antibiotic, was sometimes combined with hydroxychloroquine in early trials. However, subsequent research, including large-scale randomized controlled trials, did not find clear evidence that chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine is effective in treating COVID-19. In fact, these drugs were associated with potential side effects, including heart rhythm disturbances, especially when combined with azithromycin. Due to these safety concerns and a lack of proven benefit, major health organizations, such as the World Health Organization and national regulatory agencies, do not recommend chloroquine or azithromycin for the routine treatment of COVID-19 outside of clinical trials.

Self-medicating with prescription drugs like chloroquine and azithromycin is potentially dangerous. Both drugs require a physician’s evaluation for safe use. Azithromycin is an antibiotic, and antibiotics do not treat viral infections such as COVID-19 unless there is a confirmed bacterial co-infection. Unsupervised use can lead to adverse reactions, drug interactions, and contribute to antibiotic resistance.

The post also recommends taking zinc and vitamins C and D supplements. While these nutrients play important roles in maintaining immune function, current evidence does not support their use as a cure or specific treatment for COVID-19. Some studies have explored the potential benefit of zinc and vitamin D supplementation, particularly in patients with deficiencies; however, there is no conclusive evidence that these supplements prevent or treat COVID-19 in otherwise healthy individuals. Excessive intake of supplements can also cause harm, such as gastrointestinal distress or, in extreme cases, toxicity.

Current public health guidelines advise individuals with COVID-19 symptoms to isolate themselves to prevent the spread of the virus and to seek medical advice, especially if they have risk factors for severe disease or if symptoms worsen. Supportive care, such as rest, hydration, and over-the-counter remedies for symptom relief, is generally recommended for mild cases. Prescription medications for COVID-19 are reserved for specific patients and are only given under medical supervision.

In summary, the social media post’s advice to self-medicate with chloroquine and azithromycin, as well as to take zinc and vitamin C and D supplements, is not supported by current scientific evidence or public health guidelines. Self-medication with these drugs can be harmful, and supplements should only be used as advised by a healthcare professional. Anyone experiencing COVID-19 symptoms should follow official health recommendations and consult a physician for appropriate guidance.

Naujausia socialinio tinklo paskelbimas teigia, kad asmenys, patiriantys simptomus, susijusius su COVID-19, turi savarankiškai gydytis chlorokuinu ir azitromicinu, taip pat vartoti zinko ir C ir D vitaminų papildomų. Šis teiginys skatina konkrečių vaistų ir papildomų vartojimą kaip savarankiško valdymo būdą, susijusį su COVID-19 simptomais. Svarbu atsargiai apsvarstyti dabartinį medicinos rekomendacijų ir mokslo įrodymų, kad būtų vertinama šios patarimo tikslumas ir saugumas.

Chlorokuinas ir azitromicinas abu pirmiausiai dėmesio pritraukė COVID-19 pandemijos pradžioje. Chlorokuinas tradiciškai naudojamas malarija, o jo susijęs junginys, hidroksichlorokuinas, buvo pirmiausia tyrėjas dėl jo potencialaus antivirusinio poveikio. Azitromicinas, antibiotikas, kartais buvo derinamas su hidroksichlorokuinu ankstyvoje tyrime. Tačiau vėlesni tyrime, įskaitant didelius atsitiktinius kontrolinius tyrimus, nėra aiškaus įrodymų, kad chlorokuinas ar hidroksichlorokuinas yra efektyvus gydymas nuo COVID-19. Iš tikrųjų šie vaistai buvo susieti su potencialiais poveikiais, įskaitant širdies ritmo sutrikimus, ypač kai jie derinami su azitromicinu. Dėl šių saugumo problemų ir nesustiprinto naudos, didelės sveikatos organizacijos, tokios kaip pasaulio sveikatos organizacija ir nacionalinės reguliatorinės institucijos, nerekomenduoja chlorokuino ar azitromicino naudoti rutiniam COVID-19 gydymui, išskyrus klinikinius tyrimus.

Savarankiškai gydyti receptiniais vaistais, tokiais kaip chlorokuinas ir azitromicinas, gali būti pavojinga. Abu šie vaistai reikalauja gydytojo vertinimo, kad būtų naudojami saugiai. Azitromicinas yra antibiotikas, ir antibiotikai nėra gydymo virusinėms infekcijoms, tokios kaip COVID-19, išskyrus atvejus, kai yra patvirtinta bakterinė koinfekcija. Nenurodytoje naudojimo atveju gali kilti neigiamų reakcijų, vaistų sąveikų ir prisidėti prie antibiotikų rezistencijos.

Paskelbimas taip pat rekomenduoja zinko ir C ir D vitaminų papildomų vartojimą. nors šie mikroelementai turi svarbų vaidmenį imuninės sistemos funkcijos išlaikymui, dabartiniai įrodymai nesustiprina jų vartojimo kaip gydymo arba kūno apsaugos nuo COVID-19. Kai kurie tyrimai tyrė zinko ir vitamino D papildomų potencialinę naudą, ypač pacientams su deficitu, tačiau nėra aiškų įrodymų, kad šie papildomi medžiagos prevencija ar gydymas COVID-19 sveikiems asmenims. Per didelis vartojimas gali sukelti žalą, tokia kaip virškinimo sutrikimai arba, labiausiai ekstremaliu atveju, toksinumas.

Dabartinės viešosios sveikatos rekomendacijos pataria asmenims, patiriantiems COVID-19 simptomus, izoliuotis, kad būtų išvengta viruso skirstymosi, ir kreiptis į medicinos pagalbos, ypač jei turi rizikos veiksnių sunkiems ligos atvejams arba jei simptomai pablogėja. Dėl lengvų atvejų rekomenduojama pagalbos, tokios kaip atsargas, hidratacija ir pergalės vaistai simptomų mažinimui. Receptinės medicinos vaistai nuo COVID-19 yra rezervuoti tam tikriems pacientams ir tik naudojami medicinos įstaigų stebėjimu.

Išvados: socialinio tinklo paskelbimo patarimas savarankiškai gydytis chlorokuinu ir azitromicinu, taip pat vartoti zinko ir C ir D vitaminų papildomus, nėra pagrįstas dabartine moksline įrodymų ar viešosios sveikatos rekomendacijų. Savaugi gydymas šiais vaistais gali būti pavojingas, o papildomų vartojimas turi būti atliekamas pagal sveikatos priežiūros specialistų rekomendacijas. Kiekvienas asmuo, patiriantis COVID-19 simptomus, turi laikytis oficialių sveikatos rekomendacijų ir kreiptis į gydytoją dėl tinkamos pagalbos.

In recent days, a social media post has circulated claiming that the Governor of Bahia, a state in Brazil, dismissed a doctor who appealed to then-President Jair Bolsonaro for chloroquine. This allegation touches on several sensitive issues in Brazil, including the politicization of COVID-19 treatment and the tension between state and federal governments during the pandemic. This article examines the veracity of the claim, providing context and factual analysis.

To begin, Bahia is one of Brazil’s largest states, governed since 2015 by Rui Costa, a member of the Workers’ Party (PT), a political group often opposed to the policies of Jair Bolsonaro, who served as President of Brazil from 2019 to 2022. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Bolsonaro drew international attention for promoting the use of chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine as treatments for COVID-19, despite limited scientific evidence supporting their effectiveness. This stance often put him at odds with state governors and health authorities, who largely followed World Health Organization guidance.

The core claim revolves around a doctor in Bahia who was allegedly dismissed after appealing to Bolsonaro for chloroquine. Fact-checking this statement requires examining both the reported dismissal and the circumstances leading to it.

Throughout the pandemic, several doctors in Brazil publicly supported the use of chloroquine, some even appealing directly to Bolsonaro, who responded by promising access to the drug. In Bahia, there was at least one high-profile case involving a doctor who requested support from the federal government for chloroquine supplies, citing the drug’s use in treating COVID-19 patients.

However, the assertion that the governor personally dismissed the doctor is not substantiated by official records. The state health department did confirm that certain medical professionals were removed or reassigned from their posts during the pandemic, but these actions were generally attributed to administrative decisions or breaches of medical protocols, rather than political retribution for supporting chloroquine.

In one reported incident, a doctor working in a state-run hospital in Bahia was dismissed after publicly advocating for chloroquine and contacting federal authorities, including Bolsonaro, for assistance. According to state officials, the dismissal was based on the doctor’s failure to adhere to established treatment protocols, which did not include chloroquine due to lack of evidence. The health department maintained that the decision was based on medical guidelines, not political pressure.

It is important to note that the use of chloroquine as a COVID-19 treatment was highly contentious in Brazil. While Bolsonaro’s administration encouraged its use, many state governments, including Bahia’s, followed international health experts in discouraging it, citing potential risks and lack of efficacy.

In summary, while there is evidence that doctors in Bahia who promoted chloroquine and appealed to Bolsonaro faced dismissal or reassignment, the claim that the governor directly dismissed a doctor for appealing to the president is misleading. Dismissals were typically linked to violations of medical protocols rather than explicit political retaliation. The situation reflects broader conflicts in Brazil’s pandemic response, where political and medical guidelines often collided, but it does not fully support the specific claim made in the social media post.
