A recent social media post claims that the Italian Senate has approved a Covid-19 early treatment protocol. This assertion has gained attention, prompting questions about its accuracy and its potential implications for public health policy in Italy. To assess the validity of this claim, it is important to examine the legislative process, the nature of the protocol in question, and the broader medical and political context.

Background and Context

Since the outset of the Covid-19 pandemic, the issue of early treatment—meaning medical interventions administered during the initial phase of infection—has been a subject of debate worldwide. Early treatment protocols typically involve the use of antiviral drugs, anti-inflammatory medications, and other therapies aimed at preventing disease progression. In Italy, as in many countries, official guidance has primarily emphasized vaccination, symptomatic management, and hospitalization for severe cases.

However, some medical professionals and political groups have advocated for formal recognition of early treatment strategies. These advocates argue that prompt intervention could reduce hospitalizations and improve outcomes. The debate has played out both in the medical community and in the halls of government, including the Italian Senate.

Fact-Checking the Claim

The Italian Senate functions as the upper house of Italy’s Parliament, with the authority to debate and vote on legislation and resolutions. In recent years, the Senate has discussed various proposals related to Covid-19 management, including resolutions urging the government to update treatment guidelines.

In early 2022 and again in 2023, the Senate hosted debates regarding the use of early treatment protocols. These discussions were fueled by pressure from some senators and advocacy groups who called for a more proactive approach to treating Covid-19. The debates centered on whether the government should officially endorse protocols involving drugs such as hydroxychloroquine, ivermectin, corticosteroids, and monoclonal antibodies for use in the early stages of infection.

However, while the Senate did vote on resolutions related to Covid-19 management, these resolutions are not legally binding and do not equate to formal approval of a nationwide medical protocol. In most cases, the resolutions urged the Ministry of Health to consider updating guidelines or to take into account new evidence regarding early treatment. The Ministry of Health responded by maintaining its position that only treatments with proven efficacy, as evaluated by scientific evidence and regulatory authorities, should be recommended.

No binding law or official protocol for early treatment was enacted as a result of Senate votes. The official guidelines for Covid-19 treatment in Italy continue to be set by the Ministry of Health and are based on recommendations from medical and regulatory bodies. These guidelines focus on supportive care, use of antiviral agents in specific cases, and prompt hospitalization for worsening symptoms.

Conclusion

The core claim that the Italian Senate approved a Covid-19 early treatment protocol is misleading. While the Senate engaged in debates and passed non-binding resolutions urging consideration of early treatments, it did not formally approve or enact a specific protocol. The official stance and guidelines remain under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Health, which has not adopted widespread early treatment protocols as advocated by some senators. Social media users and the public should be aware of the distinction between parliamentary debate, non-binding resolutions, and the actual implementation of medical policy in Italy.

A claim circulating on social media states that the governors of Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo attended Carnival 2020 events even after the pandemic was officially declared. This assertion has raised questions about the conduct of state leaders during the early days of the COVID-19 pandemic. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is necessary to examine the timeline of the pandemic’s declaration, the scheduling of Carnival 2020, and the activities of the governors in question.

Carnival is one of Brazil’s most significant cultural events, attracting millions of participants and tourists every year. In 2020, Carnival festivities officially took place from February 21 to February 26. Traditionally, the governors of Brazil’s largest states—Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo—attend high-profile events during this period, both as official representatives and as part of the celebrations.

The COVID-19 pandemic was first identified in Wuhan, China, in late 2019, with global concern mounting throughout January and February 2020. The World Health Organization (WHO) declared COVID-19 a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on January 30, 2020. However, it was not until March 11, 2020, that the WHO officially characterized the outbreak as a global pandemic. In Brazil, the first confirmed case of COVID-19 was reported on February 26, 2020, coinciding with the final day of Carnival. At that time, awareness of the virus was growing, but no national or state-level emergency decrees specifically related to the pandemic had been issued.

During the week of Carnival 2020, both Wilson Witzel, then governor of Rio de Janeiro, and João Doria, then governor of São Paulo, were seen attending official and public Carnival events. Their presence at these festivities was in keeping with tradition and occurred before the pandemic was declared by the WHO. In the days following Carnival, as the first cases were confirmed in Brazil, state and municipal governments began to adopt precautionary measures, including public health advisories and, later, restrictions on large gatherings.

It is important to clarify the sequence of events: the 2020 Carnival concluded on February 26, the same day as the first confirmed COVID-19 case in Brazil, and roughly two weeks before the global pandemic declaration by the WHO. No state of emergency or lockdown had been decreed in Brazil or in the states of Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo during Carnival. The claim that the governors attended Carnival “even after the pandemic was decreed” is therefore inaccurate. At the time, there was no official pandemic declaration or local decree that would have restricted such activities.

In summary, while it is true that the governors of Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo participated in Carnival 2020 events, they did so before the pandemic was declared by international or local authorities. The implication that they ignored pandemic decrees during the celebration is not supported by the timeline of events. The claim circulating online misrepresents the facts regarding the pandemic’s declaration and the actions of the governors during the 2020 Carnival.

In recent days, a social media post has circulated claiming that the Brazilian state of Bahia eliminated its intubation waiting line for Covid-19 patients immediately following the announcement that the Brazilian Congress would investigate governors. The post suggests a direct connection between the threat of investigation and the reported improvement in Bahia’s Covid-19 healthcare response. This article examines the validity of these claims and provides necessary context.

**Background: Covid-19 Crisis in Brazil and Bahia**

Since the beginning of the Covid-19 pandemic, Brazil has faced significant challenges, including high transmission rates and overburdened healthcare systems. The Northeast state of Bahia, with a population of over 15 million, was among those hit hard during peak waves of the pandemic. Hospitals in Bahia, particularly in early 2021, struggled with shortages of ICU beds, medical supplies, and crucial medications for intubation, leading to waiting lists for patients requiring mechanical ventilation.

**The Congressional Inquiry**

In April 2021, the Brazilian Senate established a Parliamentary Commission of Inquiry (CPI) to investigate the federal and state governments’ pandemic responses, including allegations of mismanagement and misuse of Covid-19 funds. The announcement intensified scrutiny on governors, including those from opposition parties, as the federal government and certain political actors suggested state-level mismanagement had contributed to poor pandemic outcomes.

**Intubation Line in Bahia: Timeline and Causes**

The core claim of the social media post is that Bahia’s intubation line disappeared after the CPI announcement, implying causality. However, a closer look at the timeline and the underlying factors complicates this narrative.

Bahia faced a critical shortage of ICU beds and intubation drugs in March and April 2021, with reports of waiting lists for critical Covid-19 patients. The situation was widely publicized, prompting state and federal authorities to take urgent action. In late April and early May, Bahia’s state government ramped up efforts to expand ICU capacity and secure medical supplies, aided by a decrease in new Covid-19 cases due to stricter containment measures.

By mid-May 2021, Bahia’s health authorities announced that the waiting list for intubation had been cleared, attributing the improvement to the opening of new ICU beds, increased procurement of medications, and a drop in critical cases. While the congressional inquiry was announced during this period, there is no direct evidence that the investigation itself was the primary driver behind the end of the intubation line.

**Fact-Checking the Claim**

The post’s implication of a causal relationship between the congressional investigation and the clearing of the intubation line is misleading. Health experts and local officials cited the expansion of ICU capacity, improved drug supply, and a downward trend in case numbers as the main reasons for the improvement. The timing of the CPI announcement and the clearing of the intubation line may coincide, but correlation does not equal causation.

Furthermore, there is no public documentation or official statement from Bahia’s government linking the end of the intubation waiting list directly to the congressional investigation. The improvement appears to be the result of ongoing public health efforts rather than a reaction to political pressure.

**Conclusion**

While it is accurate that Bahia eliminated its intubation waiting list for Covid-19 patients during the period when the congressional investigation was announced, the assertion that this was a direct response to the investigation is unsubstantiated. The available evidence points instead to public health measures, increased resources, and a reduction in cases as the primary factors. As with many pandemic-related claims, it is important to distinguish between coincidence and causation to avoid spreading misleading information.

コロナウイルス感染症（COVID-19）のパンデミックが始まった以来、ブラジルは高感染率や医療システムの過負荷といった重大な課題に直面してきました。人口1,500万人以上の東北部州であるバハIA州も、パンデミックのピーク期に深刻な影響を受けました。2021年早春には、バハIA州の病院では集中治療室（ICU）ベッドや医療用品、気管切開に必要な薬品などの不足が深刻化し、機械換気が必要な患者の待機列が生じました。

**議会調査**

2021年4月、ブラジル上院は、パンデミック対応における連邦政府および州政府の対応、包括的に資金の誤用や管理ミスに関する告発を調査する議会特別委員会（CPI）を設置しました。この発表により、知事らへの監視が強化され、特に反対政党的な知事も含め、連邦政府と一部政治的関係者は、州レベルでの管理ミスがパンデミックの悪化に寄与したと指摘しました。

2021年3月から4月にかけて、バハIA州は集中治療室（ICU）ベッドや気管切開薬の深刻な不足に直面し、機械換気が必要なコロナウイルス患者の待機列が報告されました。この状況は広く報道され、州および連邦当局は緊急対応を開始しました。4月下旬から5月上旬には、バハIA州政府は、感染症の新しい症例数が厳格な封鎖措置によって減少したことを踏まえ、集中治療室の容量拡大や医療用品の確保に向けた取り組みを強化しました。

**主張の検証**

この投稿は、議会調査と気管切開待機列の解消との間の因果関係を示唆していますが、これは誤解を招く表現です。医療専門家や現地の官僚は、集中治療室の容量拡大、薬品供給の改善、症例数の減少が改善の主な要因であると述べています。CPIの発表と気管切開待機列の解消の時期が重なっている可能性はありますが、相関関係が因果関係であるとは限りません。

さらに、バハIA州政府からは、気管切開待機列の解消と議会調査との間の直接的な関連性を示す公的文書や公式声明は公表されていません。改善は、継続的な公衆衛生対策によるものであり、政治的圧力への反応ではないと考えられます。

**結論**

バハIA州がコロナウイルス患者の気管切開待機列を解消した時期に、議会調査が発表されたことは事実ですが、この解消が調査への直接的な反応であるという主張は裏付けられていません。現時点での証拠は、公衆衛生対策の強化、資源の増加、そして症例数の減少が主な要因であることを示しています。多くのパンデミック関連の主張においても、偶然と因果関係の区別が重要であり、誤った情報を広めないためにも、注意が必要です。

A video circulating on social media claims to showcase widespread dissatisfaction among the Argentine population with the current government. The footage, which has garnered significant attention, appears to capture scenes of protests, vocal criticism, and large gatherings of people expressing discontent. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is essential to examine both the authenticity of the video and the broader context of Argentina’s political climate.

Argentina has been undergoing a period of economic and political turmoil, particularly since the election of President Javier Milei in late 2023. Milei, a libertarian economist, was elected on a platform of radical economic reform, promising to slash government spending, eliminate deficits, and address the country’s chronic inflation. His administration quickly implemented austerity measures, including the reduction of subsidies, cuts to public sector jobs, and the loosening of currency controls. These reforms, while aimed at stabilizing the economy, have had immediate and deeply felt impacts on ordinary Argentines.

In the months following the implementation of these policies, Argentina has witnessed a notable increase in public demonstrations and strikes. Labor unions, student groups, and a range of civic organizations have organized mass protests in major cities such as Buenos Aires, Córdoba, and Rosario. Many participants voice concerns over rising unemployment, reductions in social services, and a perceived erosion of social safety nets. Images and videos of these demonstrations have been widely shared on social media, contributing to the impression of broad-based public unrest.

A viral social media post has claimed that former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro “secretly built a 5G technology and vaccine factory.” The assertion has sparked widespread speculation and debate, with some users questioning the secrecy and motivations behind such a project. This article examines the veracity of these claims, offering context and a detailed analysis of the available evidence.

Background and Context

Jair Bolsonaro served as Brazil’s president from January 2019 to December 2022. His administration was marked by controversial stances on public health, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic, and by a cautious approach to the rollout of new technologies such as 5G wireless networks. The Brazilian government, under Bolsonaro, faced criticism for delays in vaccine procurement and distribution, as well as for skepticism toward certain public health measures. Simultaneously, the global race to deploy 5G infrastructure intensified, with Brazil eventually launching a 5G spectrum auction in late 2021.

The Claim: A Secret 5G and Vaccine Factory

The core claim circulating on social media alleges that Bolsonaro secretly constructed a facility dedicated to both 5G technology and vaccine production. The post suggests that the project was deliberately hidden from the public and possibly from regulatory authorities.

Analysis

To evaluate this claim, it is necessary to consider both public records and the nature of large-scale infrastructure projects.

1. Transparency and Oversight

Major national projects such as factories—especially those involved in advanced technology or pharmaceuticals—require significant resources, regulatory approval, and oversight. In Brazil, the construction of vaccine production facilities is overseen by entities such as ANVISA (the National Health Surveillance Agency), while telecommunications infrastructure is regulated by ANATEL (the National Telecommunications Agency). No records or credible reports exist indicating that a combined 5G and vaccine facility was planned or built under Bolsonaro’s administration, either publicly or in secret.

2. Vaccine Production in Brazil

Brazil is home to renowned public biomedical institutes, such as the Butantan Institute and Fiocruz, both of which played leading roles in vaccine production and distribution during the pandemic. These institutes operate transparently and in collaboration with international partners. The Bolsonaro government did not launch independent vaccine factories, and any new facility would have required substantial investment, workforce recruitment, and regulatory approval—all activities likely to generate public records and media coverage.

3. 5G Infrastructure Development

Regarding 5G technology, Bolsonaro’s administration did oversee the launch of 5G services, primarily through partnerships with established telecommunications companies. The process was subject to public tenders and regulatory scrutiny, and there is no evidence that a dedicated government-run 5G factory was constructed, let alone one combining vaccine production.

4. Secrecy and Feasibility

The construction and operation of a large-scale factory—particularly one involved in sensitive areas such as telecommunications and pharmaceuticals—would be nearly impossible to conceal due to financial, logistical, and regulatory requirements. No whistleblowers, investigative journalists, or official records have corroborated claims of such a secret facility.

Conclusion

After a thorough review, there is no factual basis for the claim that former President Jair Bolsonaro secretly built a 5G technology and vaccine factory. The available evidence, regulatory frameworks, and transparency requirements make such a development highly implausible. The claim appears to be unfounded and lacks support from any credible sources or documentation.

Questo articolo esamina la veridicità di tali affermazioni, offrendo un contesto e un'analisi dettagliata delle prove disponibili.

Contesto e Background

Jair Bolsonaro ha ricoperto la carica di presidente del Brasile dal gennaio 2019 al dicembre 2022. Il suo governo è stato segnato da posizioni controversie riguardo alla salute pubblica, in particolare durante la pandemia di COVID-19, e da un approccio cauto verso l'introduzione di nuove tecnologie come le reti 5G wireless. Il governo brasiliano, sotto la presidenza di Bolsonaro, ha subito critiche per i ritardi nell'acquisto e nella distribuzione dei vaccini, nonché per la scetticismo verso certe misure di salute pubblica. In parallelo, la competizione globale per l'implementazione dell'infrastruttura 5G si è intensificata, con il Brasile che ha lanciato allineamenti di spettro 5G in tarda 2021.

L'Affermazione: Una Fabbrica Segreta di Tecnologia 5G e Vaccini

L'affermazione principale circolante sui social media afferma che Bolsonaro abbia costruito segretamente una struttura dedicata alla tecnologia 5G e alla produzione di vaccini. Il post suggerisce che il progetto fosse deliberatamente nascosto al pubblico e forse anche alle autorità regolamentari.

Analisi

Per valutare questa affermazione, è necessario considerare sia i documenti pubblici che la natura di grandi progetti infrastrutturali.

1. Trasparenza e Sorveglianza

Grandi progetti nazionali come le fabbriche - specialmente quelle coinvolte in tecnologie avanzate o farmaceutiche - richiedono risorse significative, approvazione regolamentare e sorveglianza. Nel Brasile, la costruzione di impianti di produzione di vaccini è supervisionata da enti come l'ANVISA (l'Agenzia Nazionale di Sorveglianza Sanitaria), mentre l'infrastruttura delle telecomunicazioni è regolata dall'ANATEL (l'Agenzia Nazionale delle Telecomunicazioni). Non esistono registri o rapporti credibili che indicano che un impianto combinato 5G e vaccini fosse stato pianificato o costruito sotto la gestione di Bolsonaro, né pubblicamente né in segreto.

2. Produzione di Vaccini nel Brasile

Il Brasile ospita istituti biomedici pubblici riconosciuti, come l'Istituto Butantan e il Fiocruz, entrambi i quali hanno svolto un ruolo di primo piano nella produzione e distribuzione di vaccini durante la pandemia. Questi istituti operano in modo trasparente e in collaborazione con partner internazionali. Il governo di Bolsonaro non ha lanciato impianti autonomi per la produzione di vaccini, e qualsiasi nuova struttura avrebbe richiesto un investimento sostanziale, reclutamento di personale e approvazione regolamentare - attività tutte probabilmente generate da registri pubblici e copertura mediatica.

3. Sviluppo dell'infrastruttura 5G

Riguardo alla tecnologia 5G, il governo di Bolsonaro ha supervisionato il lancio dei servizi 5G, principalmente attraverso partnership con aziende telefoniche esistenti. Il processo era soggetto a gare pubbliche e scrutinio regolamentare, e non esiste alcuna prova che un impianto governativo autonomo per la tecnologia 5G fosse stato costruito, tanto meno uno che combinasse la produzione di vaccini.

4. Segretezza e fattibilità

La costruzione e l'operatività di una grande fabbrica - in particolare in settori sensibili come le telecomunicazioni e i farmaceutici - sarebbero quasi impossibili da nascondere a causa dei requisiti finanziari, logistici e regolamentari. Non esistono whistleblower, giornalisti investigativi o documenti ufficiali che confermino l'esistenza di un tale impianto segreto.

Conclusione

Dopo una revisione approfondita, non c'è alcuna base fatta per l'affermazione che l'ex presidente Jair Bolsonaro abbia segretamente costruito una fabbrica di tecnologia 5G e di vaccini. Le prove disponibili, i quadri regolamentari e i requisiti di trasparenza rendono tale sviluppo altamente improbabile. L'affermazione sembra essere infondata e manca di supporto da parte di qualsiasi fonte o documento credibile.

A recent social media post claims that American research did not find the SARS-CoV-2 virus in any of the 1,500 RT-PCR tests with positive results analyzed. This statement has caused confusion and concern, as it suggests that the tests commonly used to diagnose COVID-19 may not be detecting the actual virus. This article examines the validity of the claim, provides context for how RT-PCR testing works, and analyzes the available evidence.

RT-PCR (reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction) tests have been the primary diagnostic tool for detecting SARS-CoV-2, the virus responsible for COVID-19, since the early stages of the pandemic. These tests are designed to detect the presence of specific genetic material from the virus in patient samples, usually collected via nasal or throat swabs. When a sample tests positive, it means that fragments of the virus’s RNA were found, indicating an infection.

The claim suggests that in a study involving 1,500 positive RT-PCR tests conducted in the United States, researchers failed to find any evidence of the SARS-CoV-2 virus. This interpretation contradicts both the purpose and the function of RT-PCR testing. If a test is positive, it means that the virus’s genetic material has been detected. There is no established scientific evidence or credible research indicating that American researchers analyzed 1,500 positive RT-PCR samples and found no trace of the virus.

It is possible that this misinformation stems from a misunderstanding of what RT-PCR tests detect. RT-PCR does not detect whole, live virus particles; rather, it identifies sequences of viral RNA. This distinction is important: the test cannot confirm the presence of infectious virus, only that genetic material from the virus is present. Some critics have misinterpreted this technical detail to suggest that positive tests are invalid or do not confirm infection, but this is a misrepresentation of the science.

Furthermore, the claim does not specify which "American research" it refers to, nor does it provide details about the study’s methodology, results, or publication. Such vagueness raises questions about the reliability of the statement. Throughout the pandemic, American and international research teams have consistently used RT-PCR to identify SARS-CoV-2 in positive samples, with results confirmed by genomic sequencing and viral culture in many cases.

In conclusion, the assertion that SARS-CoV-2 was not found in any of the 1,500 positive RT-PCR tests analyzed by American research is unfounded and misleading. RT-PCR is a well-established method for detecting the virus’s genetic material, and positive results are considered reliable indicators of infection. No credible scientific study supports the claim presented in the social media post. It is important to rely on verified information and understand the technical aspects of diagnostic testing to avoid spreading misinformation about COVID-19.

article_content:
A video circulating on social media claims to demonstrate that a Covid-19 test gives a positive result when exposed to water. The footage typically shows someone applying water—sometimes from a tap, bottle, or even rain—directly onto a rapid antigen Covid-19 test strip, which then displays what appears to be a positive result. This post has garnered attention and concern, with some viewers suggesting it calls into question the reliability of Covid-19 tests.

To assess this claim, it is important to understand how rapid antigen Covid-19 tests work. These tests are designed to detect specific proteins from the SARS-CoV-2 virus in samples taken from a person, usually via a nasal or throat swab. The collected sample is then mixed with a special buffer solution provided in the test kit. This buffer is a critical component: it maintains the appropriate pH and chemical conditions to enable the test to accurately detect viral proteins.

The process relies on a chemical reaction that occurs only when the buffer and the sample are used as intended. The instructions for use, included with every test kit, specify that only the provided buffer and a properly collected biological sample should be applied to the test strip. Using any other substance—including water—can disrupt the chemical environment and cause the test to malfunction.

When water is applied to a Covid-19 rapid antigen test, it does not contain the necessary chemicals to facilitate the test’s intended reaction. In many cases, water can cause the liquid to flow improperly or interact with the test strip in a way that produces lines where they should not appear. This phenomenon is known as a “false positive” or, more accurately in this context, a test malfunction or invalid result. The appearance of a positive line in these circumstances does not indicate the presence of the Covid-19 virus; rather, it is a result of improper test use.

Manufacturers and health authorities have repeatedly warned that Covid-19 rapid antigen tests are only accurate and reliable when used strictly according to the instructions. Any deviation—including the use of water, soda, juice, or other liquids—can produce misleading results that have no bearing on their effectiveness in detecting actual viral infections.

The claim that the video “shows Covid-19 test giving positive results when in contact with water” is technically accurate in the sense that a line may appear on the test strip. However, this does not reflect the test’s performance under proper conditions. Instead, it demonstrates that the test is not designed to be used with water and that misuse can cause false readings.

In summary, Covid-19 rapid antigen tests do not produce valid positive results when exposed to water. Any apparent positives in such videos are the result of improper use and do not undermine the accuracy of these tests when used as directed. The scientific consensus remains that rapid tests, when used correctly, are an effective tool for detecting Covid-19 infections.

article_content:
A social media post claims that a Stanford study found masks are ineffective against Covid-19. This assertion has circulated widely, fueling debates over public health recommendations and mask mandates. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to examine the origins of the statement, provide context about mask research, and analyze the evidence regarding mask effectiveness.

The claim appears to reference a purported Stanford study that allegedly concluded masks do not prevent the transmission of Covid-19. However, upon closer inspection, there is no record of any official Stanford University research or peer-reviewed study making such a definitive statement. The confusion largely stems from an article written by a single author, who was briefly affiliated with Stanford as a visiting scholar. The piece was published in a journal with minimal scientific oversight, and it was not a formal study endorsed by Stanford or conducted according to the university’s rigorous research standards.

Stanford University itself has publicly refuted the notion that it produced a study undermining mask effectiveness. The author’s article was an opinion piece, not original scientific research, and its conclusions contradicted the consensus of public health organizations and the broader scientific community.

It is important to consider the substantial body of research conducted globally regarding masks and respiratory virus transmission. Early in the Covid-19 pandemic, studies focused on how respiratory droplets carried the virus, leading to recommendations that masks could help reduce the spread, particularly in crowded or indoor settings. Subsequent research has continued to evaluate the effectiveness of various types of masks, including cloth masks, surgical masks, and N95 respirators.

The scientific consensus indicates that masks, while not perfect, do offer a degree of protection. They are most effective when used in combination with other preventive measures, such as vaccination, physical distancing, and proper ventilation. Masks are particularly useful in reducing the risk of transmission from individuals who are asymptomatic or pre-symptomatic, who may unknowingly spread the virus to others.

It is also worth noting that no single study can definitively prove or disprove the effectiveness of masks, as their efficacy depends on factors such as mask type, fit, duration of use, and adherence in the population. The claim that a Stanford study found masks to be “ineffective” oversimplifies the nuanced findings of many scientific investigations. Most research concludes that masks are a helpful tool in limiting Covid-19 spread, especially in settings where other interventions are not possible.

In conclusion, the social media claim that a Stanford study found masks to be ineffective against Covid-19 is misleading. The attribution to Stanford is incorrect, and the referenced article is not representative of the university’s research standards or the scientific consensus. Masks remain an important part of public health strategies to reduce Covid-19 transmission, especially when combined with other measures. Fact-checking such claims is essential to ensure the public receives accurate information during ongoing efforts to manage the pandemic.

A recent social media post has gone viral, claiming that a Brazilian doctor asserts early treatment is effective against Covid-19. The video, widely shared across multiple platforms, shows the doctor advocating for early intervention with certain medications, suggesting that such approaches can significantly reduce the severity and duration of the illness. This claim has generated considerable debate, especially among those seeking alternatives to standard Covid-19 protocols.

To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to understand what is meant by “early treatment” in the context of Covid-19. During the early phases of the pandemic, several doctors worldwide, including some in Brazil, promoted the use of various medications—most notably hydroxychloroquine, ivermectin, and azithromycin—either alone or in combination, as early interventions to prevent Covid-19 from progressing to severe disease.

Brazil became a focal point for these early treatment discussions. Some local and national authorities, as well as prominent physicians, endorsed and even distributed these medications to the public. Proponents argued that initiating treatment soon after symptom onset could blunt the virus’s impact, reduce hospitalizations, and save lives. The argument gained traction amid widespread fear and limited availability of approved therapies in the early months of the pandemic.

However, global health authorities, including the World Health Organization and national regulatory agencies, have consistently reviewed the available scientific evidence on these early treatment regimens. Large-scale clinical trials and systematic reviews have found that medications such as hydroxychloroquine and ivermectin do not provide significant benefit in preventing severe outcomes or hastening recovery from Covid-19 when used as early treatment. Some studies indicated that these drugs could even cause harm due to side effects or interactions with other medications.

Instead, the current consensus in the medical community is that early supportive care—such as rest, hydration, monitoring of symptoms, and seeking medical attention for worsening signs—remains the cornerstone of outpatient management for mild Covid-19. The development and deployment of Covid-19 vaccines, along with antiviral medications that have been rigorously tested and authorized, have proven to be more effective tools in reducing the risk of severe disease, hospitalization, and death.

It is also essential to recognize that while some individual doctors may continue to advocate for early treatment protocols based on their personal experiences or interpretations of the data, these views do not reflect the prevailing scientific consensus. The claim made by the Brazilian doctor in the video, while representing a perspective held by some during the pandemic’s early days, is not supported by the bulk of scientific evidence available as of today.

In summary, the assertion that early treatment with the medications commonly promoted in Brazil is effective against Covid-19 is not supported by high-quality clinical research. The public is advised to rely on updated guidance from reputable health authorities and to consult healthcare professionals regarding the most effective and safe treatments for Covid-19.

Kuid maailma tervishoiuorganisatsioon ja riiklikud reguleerivad asutused on järk-järgult analüüsitud kogu saadaval olevat teaduslikku tõendust neile varakate halduste kavandamiseks. Mõned uuringud näitasid, et need ravimid võivad isegi kahjulikke tagajärgi põhjustada, näiteks kõrvalmõjude või teiste medikamentidega kõrvalmõjude tõttu.

Ajalooliselt on meditsiiniasutuste praegune ükskõikus, et varakas toetav haldus – nagu ripak, veesoojendus, sümptoomide jälgimine ja meditsiinilise abi otsimine, kui sümptoomid pahenevad – on põhikindlus välisarstliku hoolduse jaoks nõrgalt süsimärkidega koroonaviiruse jaoks. article_content:
A recent social media post claims that a document proves TV Globo, one of Brazil’s largest television networks, instructed its journalists to distort pandemic data in order to attack the Bolsonaro government. This assertion has gained traction online, fueling ongoing debates over media impartiality and the politicization of COVID-19 coverage in Brazil. To assess the validity of this claim, it is essential to examine the context, background, and available evidence.

TV Globo, founded in 1965, is the most prominent broadcast network in Brazil and has historically played a significant role in shaping public opinion. Over the past few years, the network’s coverage of President Jair Bolsonaro and his government has been the subject of both praise and criticism. Bolsonaro himself has repeatedly accused Globo and other major media outlets of biased reporting, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic, when coverage of his administration’s response was frequently critical.

The claim at hand centers on the existence of a purported document allegedly instructing Globo journalists to manipulate COVID-19 data to discredit the Bolsonaro administration. Social media users have shared images and summaries of such a document, but as of this report, no verified, original document has been publicly released or authenticated. Various versions circulating online are either redacted, lack official Globo branding, or are presented without corroborating evidence of their origin or purpose.

Fact-checking initiatives and independent journalism organizations in Brazil have investigated these claims. Their findings suggest that the circulating documents lack essential verification markers, such as internal signatures, official formatting, or confirmation from current or former Globo employees. Furthermore, TV Globo has issued public statements denying the existence of any directive instructing journalists to distort pandemic data or to specifically target the Bolsonaro government in their coverage.

During the pandemic, TV Globo reported extensively on rising case numbers, vaccine developments, and the federal government’s policies. While some segments were critical of the government’s handling of the crisis—a stance shared by various international outlets—there is no concrete evidence that these reports were the result of an orchestrated campaign based on editorial orders to falsify or distort data. Editorial criticism, while sometimes harsh, is not tantamount to deliberate misinformation or manipulation.

It is also important to note that the scrutiny of government actions during a public health crisis is a core function of journalism. Journalists are expected to analyze policies, highlight shortcomings, and hold officials accountable. The existence of critical coverage does not, by itself, prove that a network is acting on political orders or intentionally distorting information.

In summary, the claim that TV Globo instructed its journalists to distort pandemic data to attack the Bolsonaro government is not supported by verified documentary evidence. The documents circulating online lack authentication, and no credible sources have substantiated the allegations. As with all viral claims, it is essential to approach such assertions with skepticism and rely on verified information.

A recent social media post claims that the Governor of São Paulo is attempting to hide an interview he gave to Chinese television. This statement has sparked speculation about the nature of the interview, the Governor’s intentions, and whether there is a deliberate effort to suppress information. To clarify the facts, it is important to examine the circumstances surrounding the interview, the Governor’s public communication strategy, and the veracity of the concealment claim.

**Background and Context**

São Paulo is Brazil’s most populous state, and its Governor frequently participates in interviews with both domestic and international media outlets. China, as one of Brazil’s major trading partners, often features in discussions about trade, investment, and diplomatic relations. Collaborative efforts between São Paulo and Chinese entities have included topics such as infrastructure, public health, and technology. Interviews with Chinese news outlets are not uncommon for Brazilian public officials seeking to promote these partnerships.

The Governor of São Paulo, whose public agenda is typically accessible through official state channels, recently participated in an interview with a major Chinese television network. The interview reportedly covered topics including bilateral cooperation, economic opportunities, and São Paulo’s response to global challenges. The appearance was part of a broader engagement with international stakeholders.

**Fact-Checking the Concealment Claim**

The central claim is that the Governor wants to hide the interview he gave to Chinese TV. To assess this, it is necessary to examine the actions taken by the Governor or his office following the interview.

First, there is no record of the Governor or his press team issuing a statement asking for the interview to be withheld or removed from public view. In fact, the Governor’s official communication channels typically share highlights from major interviews, including those with international media. There is no evidence that the Governor has requested the Chinese network to refrain from broadcasting or archiving the interview.

Second, the interview content itself does not appear to contain sensitive or controversial material that might prompt a concealment effort. The discussion focused on standard topics for international diplomacy and public relations, such as economic development, technology exchange, and pandemic management.

Third, while the interview may not have been widely promoted on the Governor’s official social media accounts or the São Paulo state government website, the absence of proactive sharing does not equate to an attempt to hide the interview. Public figures often prioritize certain media appearances over others based on strategic communication goals, audience relevance, and news cycle timing.

**Analysis and Conclusion**

There is currently no concrete evidence indicating that the Governor of São Paulo is actively trying to hide or suppress the interview he gave to Chinese TV. The lack of widespread dissemination on local channels may reflect routine media strategy rather than deliberate concealment. Furthermore, the interview remains accessible through Chinese media platforms and has not been subject to removal or restriction.

The social media post’s claim is therefore unsupported by verifiable facts. The Governor’s participation in the interview appears to be part of regular diplomatic outreach, and there is no substantiated effort to keep its contents hidden from the public. As with many viral social media claims, it is important to distinguish between speculation and evidence-based reporting to maintain informed public discourse.

A video circulating on social media claims to show empty beds in Covid-19 Intensive Care Units (ICUs) in the Brazilian state of Paraíba, suggesting that the state has “zeroed” its Covid-19 ICU occupancy. The underlying message is that Paraíba currently has no Covid-19 patients in its ICUs, implying either the end of the pandemic in the region or a dramatic improvement in the situation. This fact-checking article examines the accuracy of this claim, the context behind the video, and the current Covid-19 situation in Paraíba.

**Context and Background**

Paraíba, located in northeastern Brazil, was significantly affected by the Covid-19 pandemic, with waves of high ICU occupancy and public health challenges. Over the past year, the country has seen a reduction in severe Covid-19 cases due to vaccination campaigns, improved treatment protocols, and the natural progression of the pandemic. Social media posts related to Covid-19 hospitalizations often go viral, especially those suggesting notable changes such as the closure of ICUs or the end of emergency measures.

The video in question shows rows of unused hospital beds, purportedly filmed inside a Covid-19 ward in Paraíba. The accompanying caption claims that the state has “zeroed” its Covid-19 ICUs, meaning that there are no longer any patients requiring intensive care for Covid-19.

**Fact-Checking Analysis**

To verify the claim, it is important to assess both the authenticity of the video and the current data on Covid-19 ICU occupancy in Paraíba.

First, the video itself does appear to show an empty hospital ward. However, visual evidence alone cannot confirm the reason for the empty beds or the date of filming. Hospital wards may be empty for a variety of reasons, such as cleaning, repurposing, or temporary closure between waves of patients. There is also the possibility that the ward is being prepared for other uses or that patient numbers have declined.

Second, official statements from Paraíba’s health authorities indicate that Covid-19 ICU occupancy has drastically decreased in recent months. The reduction is attributed to the high vaccination rate and the decline in severe cases. However, health authorities caution that “zero occupancy” does not mean the pandemic is over or that the infrastructure dedicated to Covid-19 has been dismantled. Some hospitals have indeed reported days with no Covid-19 patients in their ICUs, but this situation may fluctuate depending on new variants or outbreaks.

It is also important to note that “zeroing” ICU beds for Covid-19 is a milestone celebrated by health officials, but it does not equate to the complete eradication of the virus. The state continues to monitor case numbers and maintains readiness to reactivate Covid-19 ICUs if necessary. Furthermore, hospital capacity may be reserved for other medical conditions or used as a precaution.

**Conclusion**

The claim that Paraíba has “zeroed” its Covid-19 ICUs is partially accurate. Official data confirms that the state has experienced periods with no Covid-19 patients in intensive care, and the video likely reflects this reality. However, the broader implication that the pandemic is over or that Covid-19 infrastructure has been permanently closed is misleading. ICU occupancy can fluctuate, and health authorities remain vigilant. The empty ICU beds are a positive sign of pandemic progress in Paraíba, but continued monitoring and preparedness are essential.

Claims about treatments and cures for Covid-19 have circulated widely on social media since the onset of the pandemic. A recent post asserts that chloroquine, azithromycin, ivermectin, zinc, and vitamin C can cure Covid-19. This article examines the scientific evidence behind each of these substances and evaluates the accuracy of the claim.

Chloroquine and its derivative hydroxychloroquine are antimalarial drugs that garnered intense attention early in the pandemic. Laboratory studies initially suggested they might inhibit the SARS-CoV-2 virus in cell cultures. These findings led to a surge in off-label prescribing and several high-profile endorsements. However, when tested in rigorous clinical trials involving Covid-19 patients, both chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine showed no clear benefit in reducing mortality, hospitalizations, or severe outcomes. Some studies indicated potential risks, particularly cardiac side effects, and major health authorities advised against their use outside of clinical trials for Covid-19.

Azithromycin is a commonly used antibiotic, sometimes prescribed for its anti-inflammatory properties. Early in the pandemic, it was sometimes administered alongside hydroxychloroquine in hopes of combating Covid-19. However, subsequent clinical research found that azithromycin, alone or in combination, did not improve outcomes for Covid-19 patients. As Covid-19 is a viral illness, antibiotics like azithromycin are generally ineffective unless a patient also has a bacterial co-infection.

Ivermectin, an antiparasitic medication, was promoted by some as a potential Covid-19 treatment based on preliminary laboratory studies. However, these studies involved concentrations much higher than what is safe for humans. The majority of high-quality clinical trials have found no meaningful benefit of ivermectin in preventing or treating Covid-19. Health authorities around the world have stated that ivermectin should not be used for Covid-19 outside of clinical trials.

Zinc and vitamin C are nutrients essential for immune function, and both have been investigated for their roles in supporting the immune system. Some early hypotheses suggested that supplementation could help prevent or treat Covid-19. However, studies have not demonstrated that taking zinc or vitamin C significantly alters the course of Covid-19 in the general population. While deficiencies in these nutrients can impair immune response, there is no evidence that supplementation in non-deficient individuals cures or meaningfully treats Covid-19.

The claim that chloroquine, azithromycin, ivermectin, zinc, and vitamin C cure Covid-19 is not supported by the current body of scientific evidence. While some of these substances were initially studied or used in emergency settings, further research has shown that they do not provide a cure or significant therapeutic benefit for Covid-19. Instead, treatments such as antiviral medications specifically developed for Covid-19, monoclonal antibodies, and supportive care remain the mainstays for managing the disease. Vaccination continues to be the most effective strategy for preventing serious illness and death from Covid-19.

In summary, the assertion that these five substances cure Covid-19 is inaccurate. Public health authorities encourage individuals to rely on evidence-based treatments and consult healthcare professionals for appropriate Covid-19 care.

कोरोनावायरस (कोविड-19) के उपचार और चिकित्सा के लिए कई दावे सोशल मीडिया पर पैंडेमिक के शुरुआती दिनों से व्यापक रूप से घूम रहे हैं। एक हाल के पोस्ट में दावा किया गया है कि क्लोरोक्विन, आजिथ्रोमाइसिन, आइवरमेक्टिन, जिंक और विटामिन सी कोविड-19 के इलाज कर सकते हैं। इस लेख में इन पदार्थों के पीछे वैज्ञानिक प्रमाण की जांच की गई है और इन दावों की सटीकता का मूल्यांकन किया गया है।

क्लोरोक्विन और इसका अवलोकन एचाइड्रोक्सीक्लोरोक्विन एंटीमलेरियल दवाओं हैं जो पैंडेमिक के शुरुआती दिनों में बहुत ध्यान के विषय बन गए। प्रारंभिक प्रयोगशाला अध्ययनों ने इन्हें सेल कल्चर में SARS-CoV-2 वायरस के विरोधी के रूप में संभावित रूप से रोकने के लिए सुझाव दिया। इन खोजों के कारण कोविड-19 रोगियों के लिए अनुचित उपयोग के लिए अधिक लोकप्रियता आई और कई उल्लेखनीय समर्थन भी हुए। हालांकि, जब कोविड-19 रोगियों के लिए गंभीर क्लीनिकल ट्रायल में दोनों क्लोरोक्विन और हाइड्रोक्सीक्लोरोक्विन के कोई स्पष्ट लाभ नहीं दिखा, मृत्यु दर, अस्पतालीकरण या गंभीर परिणामों में कमी के लिए। कुछ अध्ययनों में बाद के खतरों के संकेत दिखे, विशेष रूप से कार्डियक दुष्प्रभाव, और मुख्य स्वास्थ्य अधिकारियों ने कोविड-19 के अलावा क्लीनिकल ट्रायल के बाहर इनका उपयोग रोक दिया।

आजिथ्रोमाइसिन एक आम एंटीबायोटिक है, जो कभी-कभी अपनी एंटीइंफ्लेमेटरी गुणों के लिए निर्धारित किया जाता है। पैंडेमिक के शुरुआती दिनों में, इसे हाइड्रोक्सीक्लोरोक्विन के साथ एक साथ दिया जाता था, कोविड-19 के खिलाफ लड़ाई के लिए उम्मीद के लिए। हालांकि, बाद के क्लीनिकल अध्ययनों ने दिखाया कि आजिथ्रोमाइसिन, अकेले या संयोजन में, कोविड-19 रोगियों के लिए परिणामों में सुधार नहीं कर सकता। क्योंकि कोविड-19 एक विरल रोग है, एंटीबायोटिक जैसे आजिथ्रोमाइसिन आम तौर पर असर नहीं दिखाते जब तक रोगी के पास बैक्टीरियल कोइनिफेक्शन न हो।

आइवरमेक्टिन, एक एंटीपरासिटिक दवा, कुछ लोगों द्वारा कोविड-19 के इलाज के रूप में उपयोग के लिए प्रोत्साहित किया गया था, जो प्रारंभिक प्रयोगशाला अध्ययनों पर आधारित थे। हालांकि, इन अध्ययनों में मानव के लिए सुरक्षित नहीं होने वाले बहुत अधिक सांद्रता के लिए शामिल थे। अधिकांश उच्च गुणवत्ता वाले क्लीनिकल ट्रायलों ने आइवरमेक्टिन के कोविड-19 के रोकथाम या इलाज में कोई महत्वपूर्ण लाभ नहीं दिखाया। दुनिया भर के स्वास्थ्य अधिकारियों ने घोषणा की है कि आइवरमेक्टिन कोविड-19 के लिए क्लीनिकल ट्रायल के बाहर उपयोग के लिए नहीं चाहिए।

जिंक और विटामिन सी एंटीबॉडी उत्पादन के लिए आवश्यक पोषक तत्व हैं, और दोनों के रोग प्रतिरोधक प्रणाली के समर्थन के भूमिका के बारे में अध्ययन किए गए हैं। कुछ प्रारंभिक अनुमानों के अनुसार, संपूर्ण आबोह या रोग के लिए संपूर्ण के रूप में उपयोग कर सकते हैं। हालांकि, अध्ययनों ने दिखाया है कि जिंक या विटामिन सी के ले जाने के बाद कोविड-19 के बारे में जनसांख्यिकीय आबोह में कोई बदलाव नहीं होता। यद्यपि इन पोषक तत्वों की कमी रोग प्रतिरोधक प्रणाली के प्रतिक्रिया को प्रभावित कर सकती है, लेकिन अतिरिक्त लोगों में उपयोग करने के बारे में कोविड-19 के इलाज या उपचार के लिए कोई सबूत नहीं है।

क्लोरोक्विन, आजिथ्रोमाइसिन, आइवरमेक्टिन, जिंक और विटामिन सी के कोविड-19 के इलाज के लिए दावा करना वर्तमान वैज्ञानिक प्रमाण द्वारा समर्थित नहीं है। यहां तक कि इन पदार्थों में से कुछ को आपातकालीन स्थितियों में अध्ययन किया गया या उपयोग किया गया था, लेकिन आगे के अध्ययन दिखाते हैं कि इनमें से कोई भी कोविड-19 के इलाज या उपचार के लिए उपयोग कर सकता है। बजाय इसके, विशेष रूप से कोविड-19 के लिए विकसित एंटीवायरल दवाओं, मोनोक्लोनल एंटीबॉडी और समर्थन चिकित्सा बर्बाद करने के लिए आम तौर पर प्रमुख रहे हैं। टीकाकरण अभी भी कोविड-19 से गंभीर बीमारी और मृत्यु के लिए सबसे प्रभावी रणनीति है।

के रूप में एक निष्कर्ष, इन पांच पदार्थों के कोविड-19 के इलाज के लिए दावा करना असत्य है। सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य अधिकारियों ने व्यक्तिगत लोगों को आधारभूत उपचार पर निर्भर करने और कोविड-19 के उपचार के लिए चिकित्सा विशेषज्ञ से परामर्श करने के लिए प्रोत्साहित किया है।

A recent social media post claims that Switzerland recorded an increase in deaths from Covid-19 after banning hydroxychloroquine. This statement has gained attention online, raising questions about the relationship between the regulation of hydroxychloroquine and Covid-19 mortality rates in Switzerland. In this fact-checking analysis, we examine the accuracy of this claim by exploring the timeline of hydroxychloroquine regulation, Covid-19 death rates, and scientific consensus on the drug’s efficacy.

Hydroxychloroquine, an antimalarial medication, was initially considered a potential treatment for Covid-19 early in the pandemic. Enthusiasm for its use was driven by preliminary laboratory studies and anecdotal reports. However, as larger clinical trials were conducted, the evidence supporting hydroxychloroquine’s effectiveness against Covid-19 weakened. Concerns emerged regarding side effects, particularly cardiac arrhythmias, leading regulatory agencies worldwide to reassess its use.

In Switzerland, hydroxychloroquine was initially authorized for Covid-19 treatment in hospital settings. As more data became available, Swiss authorities followed the lead of the European Medicines Agency and other public health bodies by restricting its use for Covid-19 outside clinical trials. This decision was implemented in May 2020, reflecting growing international consensus on the lack of proven benefit and potential harm associated with the drug.

To evaluate the claim that Switzerland experienced an increase in Covid-19 deaths after banning hydroxychloroquine, it is important to consider the broader epidemiological context. Switzerland, like many other European countries, faced waves of Covid-19 infections in 2020 and 2021. The timing of regulatory action on hydroxychloroquine coincided with fluctuating case rates and evolving public health measures, including lockdowns, mask mandates, and the eventual rollout of vaccines.

Examining official Swiss mortality data, there was a rise in Covid-19 deaths during the autumn and winter months of 2020, following a relative lull over the summer. However, this increase mirrors trends observed in neighboring countries and is largely attributed to the seasonal resurgence of the virus, increased social interaction, and the emergence of more transmissible variants. There is no direct evidence linking the restriction of hydroxychloroquine to this rise in deaths.

The assertion that banning hydroxychloroquine led to increased mortality implies a causal relationship. However, the scientific consensus, based on large randomized controlled trials, indicates that hydroxychloroquine does not reduce mortality or prevent severe outcomes in Covid-19 patients. Health authorities, including Swissmedic, made decisions based on this evidence to prioritize patient safety and effective treatment strategies.

In summary, while Switzerland did experience an increase in deaths after restricting hydroxychloroquine use, this trend was consistent with broader epidemiological patterns rather than a consequence of the ban itself. Current scientific evidence does not support hydroxychloroquine as an effective treatment for Covid-19, and its restriction reflects worldwide best practices. The claim presented in the social media post is misleading, as it oversimplifies complex public health dynamics and disregards the evidence-based approach taken by Swiss authorities.

Viimeisenä sosiaalisessa mediassa julkaistu viesti väittää, että Sveitsissä havaittiin koronaviruksesta aiheutuneiden kuolemien lisääntyneen jälkimmäisenä, kun hydroksikloroquine-ainetta kiellettiin. Tämä väite on saanut huomiota verkossa ja aiheuttanut kysymyksiä hydroksikloroquine-ainetta koskevasta sääntelystä ja koronaviruksesta aiheutuneista kuolemista Sveitsissä. Tässä tosiasiallisen tarkastelun analyysissa tarkastellaan väitteen tarkkuutta, tarkastelemalla hydroksikloroquine-aineen sääntelyyn liittyvää ajankulu, koronaviruksen kuolemien määrää ja tieteellistä yhteisymmärrystä lääkkeen tehokkuudesta.

Hydroksikloroquine on antimalaarihoitoa, joka arvioitiin alun perin mahdolliseksi koronaviruksen hoitoon pandemian alussa. Uskottavuus sen käytölle perustui alun perin laboratorio- tutkimuksiin ja anekdotiisiin raportteihin. Kuitenkin, kun suuremmat kliiniset tutkimukset tehtiin, hydroksikloroquine-aineen tehokkuuden tukeminen heikkenee. Sydänrytmihäiriöiden mahdollisuuden huolellinen huoli johti maailmanlaajuisesti toimiviin viranomaisiin tarkastelun uudelleenarviointiin.

Sveitsissä hydroksikloroquine-aine oli alun perin sallittu sairaaloiden hoitokäytössä. Kun enemmän dataa oli saatavilla, sveitsiläiset viranomaiset seurauksena Euroopan lääkeviraston ja muiden julkisen terveydenhuollon viranomaisten linjan ja rajoittivat sen käyttöä koronaviruksen hoitokäytössä kliinisten tutkimusten ulkopuolella. Tämä päätös toteutettiin huhtikuussa 2020, mikä heijastaa kasvavaa kansainvälistä yhteisymmärrystä lääkkeen ei osoittaneen hyödyttävän ja mahdollisen haitallisuuden puolesta.

Väitteen arviointi, että Sveitsissä koronaviruksen aiheuttamien kuolemien määrä kasvoi hydroksikloroquine-aineen kieltämisen jälkeen, vaatii huomiota laajempaan epidemiologiseen kontekstiin. Sveitsi, kuten monet muut Euroopan maat, kohtasi koronaviruksen levätyksen aaltoja vuosina 2020 ja 2021. Hydroksikloroquine-aineen sääntelyn aikataulu yhtyy vaihtelijaisiin tapauksien määräihin ja kehittyneisiin julkisen terveydenhuollon toimenpiteisiin, kuten lukkoja, suojakäytävien velvoitteita ja lopulta rokotteen jakamisen aloittaminen.

Tarkastelemalla virallista sveitsiläistä kuolleisuusdataa, koronaviruksen aiheuttamien kuolemien määrä kasvoi keväällä ja talvella 2020, jäljempänä keväällä. Kuitenkin tämä lisäys vastaa huomattavasti naapuruusmaiden havaintoja ja liittyy pääosin viruksen säännölliseen uudelleenlevitäntään, lisääntyneeseen sosiaaliseen vuorovaikutukseen ja uusien, helpommasti levittävien varianttien ilmestykseen. Ei ole suoraa näyttöä, että hydroksikloroquine-aineen rajoittaminen liittyy tähän kuolemien lisääntymiseen.

Väite, että hydroksikloroquine-aineen kieltäminen johti kuolemien lisääntymiseen, olettaa syyseurannan. Kuitenkin tieteellinen yhteisymmärrys, joka perustuu suuriin satunnaisesti valituksi kontrollitutkimuksiin, viittaa siihen, että hydroksikloroquine ei vähennä kuolleisuutta tai estä vakavia seurauksia koronaviruksen potilaiden keskuudessa. Terveydenhuollon viranomaiset, mukaan lukien Sveitsin lääkevirasto, tekivät päätökset tämän tiedon pohjalta, jotta saataisiin prioriteetti potilaiden turvallisuuden ja tehokkaan hoitokäytösten kannalta.

Yhteenvetona, vaikka Sveitsissä todettiin kuolemien lisääntyneen hydroksikloroquine-aineen käytön rajoittamisen jälkeen, tämä trendi vastaa laajempaa epidemiologista mallia, ei kuitenkaan syytä sen kieltämiseen. Nykyinen tieteellinen tieto ei tue hydroksikloroquine-aineen tehokkuutta koronaviruksen hoitoon, ja sen rajoittaminen heijastaa maailmanlaajuisia parhaita käytäntöjä. Sosiaalisessa mediassa esitettävä väite on harhaanjohtava, koska se yksinkertaistaa monimutkaista julkisen terveydenhuollon dynaamiaa ja jättää huomiotta Sveitsin viranomaisten tieteellisen perustan pohjalta tehtyjä päätökset.

The debate surrounding the scope of Brazil's Covid-19 Parliamentary Commission of Inquiry (CPI) has been a focal point in the country’s political landscape. The commission, established by the Federal Senate in April 2021, was tasked with investigating federal government actions and expenditures related to the Covid-19 pandemic. The scope of the investigation, however, quickly became a subject of controversy, particularly regarding whether state governors should also be scrutinized. In this context, a claim surfaced on social media stating that Senator Simone Tebet said, "Covid-19 Parliamentary Commission of Inquiry should not investigate governors."

To assess the accuracy of this statement, it is essential to understand the context in which Senator Simone Tebet expressed her views, as well as the broader debate about the CPI's mandate.

Senator Simone Tebet, a prominent member of the Brazilian Senate and former presidential candidate, was vocal during the formation of the Covid-19 CPI about maintaining the commission’s focus on the federal government. Her position reflected a widespread sentiment among many senators who argued that the CPI, as a legislative body at the federal level, should primarily oversee federal actions and expenditures, rather than those of state governors. This viewpoint was rooted in constitutional principles regarding the separation of powers and the jurisdiction of parliamentary inquiries.

Tebet’s public statements at the time highlighted her concerns that expanding the CPI’s scope to include governors would politicize the investigation, dilute its effectiveness, and potentially distract from the central question of federal accountability during the pandemic. She argued that the Federal Senate lacked the constitutional authority to investigate state executives directly, as such oversight falls within the purview of state legislatures and local agencies. This was a key point in the legal and political debate surrounding the CPI’s powers.

As the commission proceeded, there was considerable pressure from some political factions, including allies of President Jair Bolsonaro, to include governors in the investigation. They argued that corruption and mismanagement of pandemic funds occurred at all levels of government and that the CPI should be comprehensive in its approach. However, Tebet and others maintained that the primary purpose of the commission was to examine federal decision-making, procurement, and distribution of pandemic resources.

Analysis of the claim that Senator Simone Tebet said "Covid-19 Parliamentary Commission of Inquiry should not investigate governors" shows it aligns with her publicly stated position during the CPI discussions. While she did not categorically deny the possibility of state-level investigations, her stance was clear that the Federal Senate’s commission was not the appropriate venue for such inquiries. Tebet advocated for a focused federal investigation, while recognizing that state legislatures could independently pursue oversight of governors if warranted.

In conclusion, the social media post accurately reflects Senator Simone Tebet’s position during the debate over the Covid-19 Parliamentary Commission of Inquiry’s scope. Her arguments were grounded in constitutional considerations and concerns about the efficacy and impartiality of the investigation. The controversy underscored broader tensions in Brazilian politics over accountability for the pandemic response, and continues to be a point of discussion as the country evaluates the lessons learned from its handling of the crisis.

Braziliyanın Pandemiyadan Keçmiş Dövlət Komissiyasının (CPI) məsuliyyət sahəsinin müzakirəsi, ölkənin siyasi mərkəzi oldu. 2021-ci il aprelində Federal Senat tərəfindən yaradılmış bu komissiya, federal dövlət hökumətinin pandemiyadan ələ keçirilmiş əməliyyatlar və xərclərini araşdırmaq üçün yaradılmışdı. Lakin araşdırmanın məsuliyyət sahəsi çox sürətli olaraq məsələlərə səbəb oldu, xüsusən də, xalq sədərlərini də nəzərə almaq məsələsi. Bu bağlamda sosial media-da bir iddia ortaya çıxdı ki, senator Simone Tebet "Pandemiyadan Keçmiş Dövlət Komissiyası xalq sədərlərini araşdırmaqda istifadə etməlidir" dedi.

Bu iddianın doğru olub-olmamasını müəyyən etmək üçün senator Simone Tebetin fikirlərini ifadə etdiyi mədəniyyət və CPI-nin məsuliyyət sahəsi üsulu barədə daha əhəmiyyətli müzakirələri nəzərə almaq vacibdir.

Senator Simone Tebet, Braziliyanın əsas senatorlarından və keçmiş prezident seçilməyə çalışmış bir məşhur şəxsdir. Pandemiyadan Keçmiş Dövlət Komissiyası yaradılma prosesində onun fikirləri, komissiyada federal dövlət hökumətinin məsuliyyət sahəsinin qorunması ilə bağlı ciddi ifadələr etdi. Onun pozisiyası, senatorlər arasında yaygındır, ki, Pandemiyadan Keçmiş Dövlət Komissiyası, federal səviyyədə bir qanunvericilik təşkilatı olduğuna görə, əsasən federal əməliyyatlar və xərclərini nəzərdən keçirməlidir, xalq sədərlərinin əməliyyatlarını isə nəzərə almaqda. Bu fikir, qanunvericilik qaydaları və parlamentar araşdırmaların məsuliyyət sahəsi ilə bağlı konstitusiyalı məsələlərə əsaslanırdı.

Tebetin əsas fikirləri, komissiyada xalq sədərlərini də nəzərdən keçirmək, araşdırmayı siyasiyyətə çevirəcək, effektivliyini azaldacaq və pandemiyada federal məsuliyyət məsələsindən çıxaracaq. Onun fikrini, Federal Senatın xalq sədərlərini doğrudan araşdıra bilmədiyini, bu nəzarət xalq sədərlikləri və yerli təşkilatların məsuliyyət sahəsindədir. Bu, CPI-nin məsuliyyət sahəsinin məsələlərində əsas fikirlərdir.

Komissiya prosesində, bir çox siyasi qruplar, də, prezident Jair Bolsonaro-nun dostları, xalq sədərlərini də araşdırmaqda əsaslı təzyiq təqdim etdi. Onlar, pandemiyadan ələ keçirilmiş fondların çox səviyyədə yolsuzluq və qərar verilməsi xətaları baş verdiyini iddia etdi və CPI-nin bütün səviyyələrdə təkamül etməlidir. Lakin Tebet və digərləri, komissiyanın əsas məqsədi federal qərar verilməsi, alınmış mənbələr və pandemiyada təqdim edilmiş resursların təqdimatı üçün araşdırmaq idi.

"Senator Simone Tebet 'Pandemiyadan Keçmiş Dövlət Komissiyası xalq sədərlərini araşdırmaqda istifadə etməlidir' dedi" iddiasının analizi, Tebetin CPI müzakirələrində ifadə etdiyi mədəniyyət pozisiyasına uyğun gəlir. Onun, xalq sədərləri üzrə araşdırmaların mümkün olmadığını təsdiqləməyən, lakin Federal Senat komissiyasının bu nəzarət üçün uyğun olmadığını bildirən fikri əsaslıdır. Tebet federal araşdırmanın əsas məqsədini təqdim etdi, xalq sədərlərinin məsuliyyət sahəsində qanunvericiliklərin hər hansı bir tələbə uyğun olarsa, xalq sədərləri öz məsuliyyət sahəsində nəzarət etməyə davam edəcək.

Nəticədə, sosial media-da yer alan iddia, senator Simone Tebetin Pandemiyadan Keçmiş Dövlət Komissiyasının məsuliyyət sahəsi müzakirəsi zamanı fikrini tam dəqiq əks etdirir. Onun fikirləri, qanunvericilik məsələləri və araşdırmanın effektivliyinə və nəzərdən keçirilməyənliyinə dair xüsusi qorxmalarla əsaslandırılmışdır. Bu məsələ, pandemiyada cavab verilməyə dair daha əsaslı siyasi çatışmaları əks etdirərək, ölkənin pandemiyadan ələ keçirilmiş məsələlərə dair əldə etdiyi təcrübələri müzakirə etməkdə davam edir.

During the Covid-19 pandemic, Brazil experienced intense political scrutiny over its public health response, culminating in the establishment of the Covid-19 Parliamentary Commission of Inquiry (CPI). The CPI, convened in 2021 by the Federal Senate, sought to investigate alleged governmental mismanagement regarding the pandemic, including delays in vaccine procurement, dissemination of misinformation, and controversial policy decisions. The commission summoned several key figures, among them Nelson Teich, who briefly served as Minister of Health from May 2020, to provide testimony.

A social media post recently claimed that Nelson Teich, during his CPI hearing, stated that senators "would root for chaos." The post implies that Teich accused members of the inquiry of actively hoping for negative developments related to the pandemic, a serious allegation that, if true, would reflect deep political polarization and undermine the impartiality expected of such an investigative body.

To fact-check this claim, it is necessary to examine the context and content of Teich’s testimony. On May 5, 2021, Nelson Teich appeared before the Covid-19 CPI. His testimony was part of a broader effort to clarify the circumstances surrounding his resignation as Minister of Health and to shed light on the federal government’s strategy for handling Covid-19. Throughout the hearing, Teich described difficulties in policy alignment and communication with President Jair Bolsonaro, particularly regarding drug recommendations and public health measures.

The claim that Teich accused senators of "rooting for chaos" appears to stem from a specific exchange during the hearing. According to available records and transcripts, Teich expressed concern about the politicization of the pandemic response. He remarked that, in some political environments, there is a tendency for groups to hope for negative outcomes to discredit opponents. However, a thorough review of the hearing indicates that Teich did not directly state that the senators themselves "would root for chaos." Rather, he made a more general observation about political dynamics, suggesting that political actors—without specifying the CPI members—sometimes benefit from chaos or crisis when it serves their agenda.

Teich’s actual words during the hearing were measured; he advocated for unity and evidence-based decision-making, emphasizing that public health should not be politicized. While he acknowledged that political interests could interfere with effective responses, he stopped short of making direct accusations against the CPI senators. The phrase "root for chaos" in the social media post appears to be a paraphrase or interpretation rather than a verbatim quote.

In conclusion, the claim that Nelson Teich said senators "would root for chaos" during his Covid-19 CPI testimony is misleading. While Teich did discuss the dangers of politicizing the pandemic and referenced the idea that some may benefit politically from chaos, he did not directly accuse the senators of the inquiry of such behavior. The social media post exaggerates and distorts his actual statements, reflecting the charged atmosphere surrounding the investigation. Fact-checking reveals that Teich’s testimony was more nuanced, focusing on the need for collaboration and evidence-based policy rather than direct condemnation of the CPI members.

કોરોનાવાયરસ મહામારી દરમિયાન બ્રાઝિલની સારવાર પ્રતિસાદ પર તીવ્ર રાજકીય નિરીક્ષણ થયું હતું, જેનો પરિણામ તરીકે કોરોનાવાયરસ પ્રાથમિક સાંચો કમિટી (CPI)ની સ્થાપના થઈ હતી. 2021માં ફેડરલ સેનેટ દ્વારા સંગ્રહિત CPIએ પ્રમુખની મહામારીની સારવાર પર અસરકારક પ્રશાસનની અસરની તપાસ કરવાનો પ્રયત્ન કર્યો હતો, જેમાં વેક્સીનની ખરીદીમાં વલણ, ખોટી માહિતીની વિતરણ અને વિવાદાસ્પદ નીતિનિર્ણયની આશંકાઓ સામેલ હતી. આ કમિટીએ કેટલાક મહત્વપૂર્ણ વ્યક્તિઓને, જેમાં મે 2020માં સારવાર મંત્રી તરીકે સાંચો કરેલા નેલ્સન ટીચને સાક્ષી આપવાની માંગ કરી હતી.

સામાજિક મીડિયા પર એક જાહેરાત માટે કહેવામાં આવી હતી કે નેલ્સન ટીચે તેના CPI સાક્ષી સંદર્ભે કહેલું હતું કે "સભ્યોએ અસ્થિરતા માટે પોતાનો સમર્થન કરશે." આ જાહેરાત સૂચવે છે કે ટીચે તપાસના સભ્યોની વિરુદ્ધ નકારાત્મક વિકાસની આશા રાખવાની આશંકા કરી હતી, જે મુખ્યત્વે સાર્વાધિકારી વિભાજન અને આવા તપાસ સંસ્થાની અસરકારકતાને નિર્ધારિત કરવા માટે ગંભીર આશંકા છે.

આ દાવાની સાચી તપાસ કરવા માટે ટીચના સાક્ષીના સંદર્ભ અને માહિતીની જરૂર છે. 5 મે 2021ના રોજ નેલ્સન ટીચે કોરોનાવાયરસ CPI સામે સાક્ષી આપી હતી. તેની સાક્ષી તેના મંત્રી તરીકે રાખેલ પદના તાજેતરના પ્રસંગના સ્પષ્ટીકરણનો ભાગ હતો અને કેન્દ્રીય સરકારની કોરોનાવાયરસની સારવાર સંદર્ભે નીતિ પર સ્પષ્ટતા આપવાનો ભાગ હતો. સાક્ષીના સમયગાળામાં, ટીચે પ્રમુખ જેર બોલ્સોનારો સાથે નીતિ અને સારવાર પ્રવાહની અસરકારકતાના સંદર્ભમાં મુશ્કેલીઓની ચર્ચા કરી હતી, ખાસ કરીને દવાના પ્રસ્તાવની અને જનસાંસ્થાની સારવાર માપદંડની સંદર્ભમાં.

ટીચે સભ્યોની "અસ્થિરતા માટે સમર્થન કરશે" દાવાની કલ્પના તેના સાક્ષી સમયગાળામાં એક વિશેષ વાતના સંદર્ભમાં આવી હતી. ઉપલબ્ધ રેકોર્ડ અને ટ્રાન્સક્રિપ્ટ મુજબ, ટીચે પ્રમાણભૂત સારવાર પ્રતિસાદની રાજકીય પ્રસ્તુતિ પર ચિંતા વ્યક્ત કરી હતી. તેમણે જણાવ્યું હતું કે કેટલાક રાજકીય વાતાવરણમાં, કેટલાક સમૂહોની નકારાત્મક વિકાસની આશા રાખવાની પ્રવૃત્તિ હોય છે જે પોતાના પ્રતિદ્વંદીઓને અસર કરે છે. તેમાંથી એક પૂર્ણ તપાસ દર્શાવે છે કે ટીચે સભ્યોની પોતાની વિરુદ્ધ સીધી રીતે "અસ્થિરતા માટે સમર્થન કરશે" કહેવું નહીં કર્યું હતું. તેમણે એક વિસ્તારિત રાજકીય વાતાવરણની માન્યતા કરી હતી, જે પ્રમાણભૂત રાજકીય ક્રિયાઓને પોતાના મંત્રીઓને વિશેષ કરીને નકારાત્મક પરિસ્થિતિઓ અથવા ક્રિસિસની આશા કરવાની ક્ષમતા રાખે છે તેની સંદર્ભમાં કહેવું છે.

સંક્ષેપમાં, નેલ્સન ટીચે CPI સાક્ષી દરમિયાન સભ્યોની "અસ્થિરતા માટે સમર્થન કરશે" કહેવું એ ભ્રમાંદોષ છે. ટીચે પ્રમાણભૂત સારવારની રાજકીય પ્રસ્તુતિની ખતરનાકતા વિશે ચર્ચા કરી હતી અને કેટલાક રાજકીય માંગણોની અસર કરવા માટે અસ્થિરતાની આશા રાખવાની વિચારણાનો સંદર્ભ આપ્યો હતો, પરંતુ તેમણે CPI સભ્યોની પોતાની વિરુદ્ધ પ્રવૃત્તિ માટે સીધો આરોપ મૂકી ન હતો. સામાજિક મીડિયા પર આ જાહેરાત તેના વાક્યને વધારે અથવા કમ સમજાવે છે, જે તપાસના સંદર્ભમાં ઉભા થયેલ તાણોને દર્શાવે છે. સાચી તપાસ દર્શાવે છે કે ટીચે સાક્ષી સમયગાળામાં સહકાર અને પ્રમાણભૂત નીતિ પર ધ્યાન આપવાની જરૂરિયાત પર ધ્યાન આપ્યું હતું, નહીં કે CPI સભ્યોની સીધી નિંદા કરી હતી.

ဒေါ်ရွန်ဂျော်လ်ဗားသည် ဒေါ်ဒိုလ်ရွန်ဂျော်လ်ဗားကို မွေးဖွားခဲ့သည်။ မိတ္တူးအောင်မြင်သော ဘရာဇ်းယား ကာကွယ်ရေးသား နှင့် အမျိုးသမီးပညာရှင် ဖြစ်သည်။ သူမ၏ အလုပ်အကိုင်ကို ၈၀ နှစ်ကျော် အကြာကြိုးတွင် ကျော်လွန်ခဲ့ပြီး သူမသည် ၂၀၀၈ ခုနှစ်တွင် ၁၀၁ နှစ်အရွယ်တွင် သေဆုံးခဲ့သည်။ သူမသည် ပြစ်မှုကျူးလွန်ခြင်း ကို စိတ်ကူးယဉ်ခြင်း နှင့် အသံုးအနှီး ပြုလုပ်ခြင်း အားဖြင့် ဘရာဇ်းယားနိုင်ငံတွင် ယဉ်ကျေးမှုအခြေခံ ပုဂ္ဂိုလ်ရေးကို ဖန်တီးခဲ့သည်။ သူမ၏ သမီးတစ်ယောက်ကို ဒိုက်မာရွန်ဂျော်လ်ဗားကို မွေးဖွားခဲ့ပြီး သမီးမြောက်သူများကို သိရှိရန်အတွက် အချက်အလက်များ သိပ်မရှိပါ။

article_summary: Um post viral afirma que a neta da atriz brasileira Dercy Gonçalves compareceu a um evento de vacinação usando uma camiseta com a frase "Fuck Lula", mas não há evidências concretas para comprovar a alegação. A falta de informações públicas sobre a família de Gonçalves e o contexto político polarizado no Brasil sugerem que a história pode ser uma fake news, alimentada por discursos contundentes e a notoriedade da figura. A análise indica que o episódio não é verificável e provavelmente foi divulgado para inflamar discussões políticas.
post_content: Granddaughter of Brazilian actress Dercy Gonçalves went to get vaccinated wearing a T-shirt with the sentence "Fuck Lula."

article_content:
In recent days, a social media post has circulated alleging that João Doria, the Governor of São Paulo, deliberately postponed his COVID-19 vaccination appointment to avoid receiving the Coronavac vaccine, opting instead for a dose of Pfizer’s vaccine. This claim has sparked debate and speculation regarding the integrity of the vaccination process among public officials in Brazil.

In recent days, a social media post has circulated claiming that former Brazilian Health Minister Eduardo Pazuello stated he did not wear his military uniform to the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry (CPI) to avoid "gazelle fetish." This peculiar phrase has drawn public attention and sparked curiosity regarding its origins, accuracy, and context. This article aims to fact-check the claim, provide background information, and clarify the circumstances surrounding Pazuello’s statement.

Eduardo Pazuello, a general in the Brazilian Army, served as Brazil’s Health Minister during a critical period of the COVID-19 pandemic. His tenure was marked by controversy, including criticism of the government’s pandemic response and logistical challenges related to vaccine distribution and oxygen shortages. In May 2021, Pazuello was summoned to testify before the Senate’s Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry, which was investigating the federal government’s management of the pandemic.

As a military officer serving in a civilian governmental role, Pazuello’s choice of attire for his CPI appearance became a matter of public debate. Traditionally, active-duty military personnel attending official proceedings may wear their uniforms. However, in this instance, Pazuello appeared in civilian clothing. The decision prompted questions from senators and journalists about why he opted not to wear his uniform, considering his rank and status.

During his testimony, Pazuello explained that he chose not to wear his uniform to avoid drawing unnecessary attention or making his military status a focal point of the proceedings. According to widely shared video excerpts and transcripts of the session, Pazuello used the expression “fetiche de gazela” (translated as “gazelle fetish”) to describe what he considered excessive or misplaced fascination with his military attire. He suggested that some individuals were overly fixated on whether he would appear in uniform, implying that it was a distraction from the substantive issues at hand.

The phrase “gazelle fetish” is not a standard idiom in Portuguese or English and appears to be a colloquialism or personal expression used by Pazuello. Its meaning in this context is not entirely clear, but it likely refers to a trivial or superficial obsession, as gazelles are sometimes associated with flightiness or distraction. Pazuello’s remarks were widely reported in Brazilian media at the time, and his use of the phrase became a subject of humor and debate on social networks.

Fact-checking analysis confirms that the core claim of the social media post is accurate: Eduardo Pazuello did, in fact, state that he refrained from wearing his uniform to the CPI to avoid "gazelle fetish." The statement reflects his view that excessive attention was being paid to his military attire rather than the substantive issues under discussion. While the phrase itself is unusual and not standard usage, it was indeed used by Pazuello in the context described.

In conclusion, the social media post correctly quotes Eduardo Pazuello’s explanation for not wearing his military uniform to the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry. The background and context support the accuracy of the claim, although the expression “gazelle fetish” remains a personal and somewhat ambiguous choice of words by the former minister. The episode highlights the intersection of military and civilian roles in government and the public’s fascination with symbolic gestures during high-profile political events.

ادواردو پاسوللو، یک سرکردۀ ارتش برزیل، در دوران بحرانی کرونا در کشور به عنوان وزیر بهداشت خدمت کرد. دوره خدمتش با تنش‌ها و انتقادات مربوط به پاسخ دادن به بحران کرونا و چالش‌های لجستیکی مرتبط با توزیع واکسن و کمبود اکسیژن همراه بود. در مه ۲۰۲۱، پاسوللو به عنوان شاهدی به جلسه کمیسیون پارلمانی بررسی که به بررسی مدیریت دولت مرکزی در برابر کرونا پرداخته بود، پیش‌روی کرد.

در طول شهادت خود، پاسوللو توضیح داد که به دلیل اجتناب از توجه ناخواسته یا تأکید بر موقعیت نظامی خود در جلسات، از پوشیدن شلوار نظامی خود خودداری کرده است. با توجه به اقتباس‌های ویدئویی و متن‌های جلسه منتشر شده، پاسوللو عبارت "فطره گزیل" (که به معنی "فطره گزیل" ترجمه شده) را برای توصیف توجه بیش از حد یا نادرست به شلوار نظامی خود استفاده کرد. او ا暗示 کرد که برخی افراد به اندازه کافی به این موضوع توجه می‌کردند و این موضوع از مسائل اصلی جلسه مانع می‌شد.

عبارت "فطره گزیل" در زبان پرتغالی یا انگلیسی به عنوان یک عبارت استاندارد وجود ندارد و به نظر می‌رسد که این عبارت یک عبارت سرگرمی یا شخصی است که پاسوللو به کار گرفته است. معنی این عبارت در این زمینه کاملاً مشخص نیست، اما احتمالاً به یک توجه بیش از حد یا سطحی اشاره دارد، زیرا گزیل‌ها اغلب با فرار یا توجه ناخواسته مرتبط هستند. اظهارات پاسوللو در زمان انتشار در روزنامه‌های برزیلی گزارش شد و استفاده از این عبارت به عنوان موضوعی برای خنده و بحث در شبکه‌های اجتماعی شد.

تحقيق درستي تأیید می‌کند که اصلی ترین ادعا در پست شبکه اجتماعی درست است: ادواردو پاسوللو در واقع اعلام کرده است که به دلیل "فطره گزیل" از پوشیدن شلوار نظامی خود در CPI خودداری کرده است. این اظهار نظر به نظر می‌رسد که نظر او در مورد توجه بیش از حد به شلوار نظامی خود در مقابل مسائل اصلی مورد بحث است. با این حال، این عبارت خود به نظر می‌رسد غیر معمول و استاندارد نیست، اما در زمینه اشاره شده توسط پاسوللو استفاده شده است.

در نهایت، پست شبکه اجتماعی به درستی اظهار نظر ادواردو پاسوللو در مورد عدم پوشیدن شلوار نظامی خود در جلسه کمیسیون پارلمانی بررسی را نقل کرده است. زمینه و زمینه‌های این ادعا به درستی این ادعا را تأیید می‌کند، اگرچه عبارت "فطره گزیل" به عنوان یک انتخاب کلمات شخصی و ممکن است مبهم توسط وزیر پیشین توضیح داده شده است. این رویداد به نشان دادن متقاطع بودن نقش‌های نظامی و مدنی در حکومت و جذب عمومی به حرکت‌های نمادین در رویدادهای سیاسی مهم توجه می‌کند.
